articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

Editorial Context: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.
• The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

articles.title: 10 patented technologies handed over to various firms at T.N. Tech Transfer Summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inaugurating the Summit, P. Viswanathan, Higher Education Minister, says it will be made into an annual affair and will be taken to other major cities in Tamil Nadu as well

Students of Classes VII and IX of the Coimbatore Public School have developed a fruit harvesting toolkit for coffee cherries. On Thursday, their innovation, for which they have applied for a patent on June 25, 2026, was passed on to a start-up firm for commercialisation.

The toolkit has a hollow pipe attached to a harvesting head that has a set of blades to cut off the ripe coffee cherries. The set of blades arranged in V-shape are guided by a push-pull casting while harvesting. The picked cherries glide through the hollow flexible hose into a storage container. The purpose of the innovation was to increase the efficiency and speed of fruit harvesting operations in plantations. This was one of the 10 products for which technology transfer took place at the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit 2006, organised jointly by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology (TNSCST) and Anna University.

S.A. Nirmala, correspondent, Coimbatore Public School, said that every year, the students work on a real-life problem that is brought in either by parents or the community. This prototype was the product of one such problem brought in by a parent. The technology was transferred to Nexorasai Pvt. Ltd., a startup firm started by the parent. Before the handover, students tested the prototype at a coffee plantation for efficacy, she said.

Among the new innovations are a drone-based infrastructure cleaning system developed by Anna University, a sanitary napkin vending machine developed by VIT Chennai, foxtail millet cookies technology, millet muesli, banana stem juice, and low-fat dessicated coconut chips technology.

S. Vincent, member secretary, TNSCST, said a total of 97 innovative technologies had emerged from higher education institutions in the State which were ready to be transferred for commercialisation. While only 10 technologies were transferred to start-ups and MSMEs for commercialisation, at least 60 industry representatives had participated at the Summit and had shown interest in the innovations.

Inaugurating the Summit, P. Viswanathan, Higher Education Minister, said it would be made into an annual affair and would be taken to other major cities in Tamil Nadu as well. He released a book titled A Compendium of Registered Geographical Indications of Tamil Nadu documenting the State’s heritage of traditional products and indigenous knowledge.

Researchers at IIT-Madras have developed a software to help identify items for probable GI registration and also address post-GI challenges such as marketing of the produce and maintaining its authenticity. Utthan India, a non-governmental organisation, working with tribal communities across India, will provide scientific and technological intervention to address problems faced by these communities. The TNSCST signed memoranda of understanding with the two institutions. Another MoU with Asian Research Association envisages training programmes for students in the State to write scientific papers.
Dheeraj Kumar, Higher Education Secretary, V. Kumaresan, Registrar-in-charge, Anna University, and A. Ramanan, Scientific Officer, TNSCST, also spoke.

articles.title: Dr. NTRUHS plans AI-based courses in affiliated colleges to strengthen research collaboration
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The university examining the feasibility of introducing interdisciplinary certificate and diploma programmes in emerging areas of health sciences

Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences (NTRUHS) is planning to introduce new academic programmes incorporating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), while strengthening research collaboration among its affiliated medical colleges.
The proposals were discussed at a meeting of principals, academic vice-principals and research committee members of affiliated medical colleges, held at the university on Thursday.

Vice-Chancellor P. Chandrasekhar said medical education must keep pace with technological advancements and changing healthcare needs. He said medical institutions should take advantage of the opportunities emerging from the State’s technology initiatives by working closely with engineering colleges, research organisations and industry.

The meeting discussed a proposal to establish a university-wide Research and Innovation Network by bringing together research facilities and the Department of Health Research and Indian Council of Medical Research-supported Multidisciplinary Research Units (MRUs) functioning in affiliated medical colleges.

The proposed network would help institutions share expertise, undertake collaborative and multicentric research projects and address healthcare challenges through coordinated research efforts, according to a release by the university.
The university is also examining the feasibility of introducing interdisciplinary certificate and diploma programmes in emerging areas of health sciences.

The meeting also discussed the proposed Amaravati School of Bio-Design, which seeks to bring medical professionals, engineers, researchers and technology institutions onto a common platform to develop innovative healthcare solutions.

The initiative is envisaged as part of the emerging innovation ecosystem associated with Amaravati Quantum Valley and Bio Valley. It would focus on identifying real-world healthcare problems and developing solutions through biomedical design, engineering and technology, the participants discussed.
The school has been proposed at the Vivenns campus in Mayuri Tech Park, Mangalagiri, with its inauguration planned for December 7, 2026.
Possibilities for collaboration with IIT Tirupati and other technical institutions were also discussed, particularly in biomedical research, medical device development and healthcare technology.

articles.title: Akvan may spare most of Andhra Pradesh; red alert issued for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, says IMD

Even as the severe cyclonic storm Akvan may spare most of Andhra Pradesh and make landfall along the south Odisha coast near Gopalpur on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has put the Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts bordering Odisha on a red alert.

Between 8.30 a.m. and 7 p.m. on Thursday, many weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded only light to moderate rain of below 35 mm. However, IMD, Amaravati, Director K. Naga Ratnam told The Hindu that the rainfall may increase from the midnight and may continue till Friday noon or evening. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is likely in these two districts.

Gales of 90 kmph to 100 kmph are also likely along the coast in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh around the midnight. Already, strong winds of 50 kmph to 60 kmph are prevailing along the coast, the Director said.

Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may also record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, but the rest of the State may not see any rainfall activity on Friday.

Weather experts said while the weather system may move closer to the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha, which is around 180 km from Srikakulam, there is a slight possibility of the system making landfall near the extreme end of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh as well.

articles.title: Repository to catalogue research occurring at institutions in T.N. to be set up, says Higher Education Secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He announces that Anna University has been asked to take the lead in developing this digital platform

The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department will soon be starting a central digital repository of all research and innovation that are taking place in higher education institutions in the State, Higher Education Secretary Dheeraj Kumar said on Thursday.

Speaking at the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit 2026 organised jointly by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology (TNSCST) and Anna University, Mr. Kumar said the repository would serve as a platform that would link various universities and institutions carrying out research and innovation in various fields, the industry, and the governmental and non-governmental organisations working with the innovators.

Later, elaborating on the initiative, he told The Hindu , “Development of technology generally gets spurred by a problem statement. Instead of doing the research ab initio , it is possible that some research would have already happened in certain universities of our State or some research institutions or centres that will be relevant to the solution that is now being sought. The point is to connect them.”

Mr. Kumar said Anna University had been asked to take the lead in developing the digital platform. “They have three incubation centres. We thought of looking at the domains that are industry-oriented that can be pushed first,” he added.

The initiative will entail the creation of a portal where all research work being carried out in universities and research institutions and innovative pursuits at incubation centres would be catalogued and put up. It will act as a common interface for stakeholders involved in the State’s innovation journey, from incubation to commercialisation, said V. Kumaresan, Registrar-in-charge, Anna University.

Explaining further, he said if a business house or a start-up firm is looking for a specific technology or process, instead of running from pillar to post they could visit the portal and tap into the research work being carried out by institutions across the State. “It will help the State to identify areas where we are s t rong, research areas where the universities are working, and the possible avenues for innovation,” Dr. Kumaresan added.

articles.title: Tension in Pulivendula for third day as TDP, YSRCP spar over ‘poll violence’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tense moments prevailed for the third consecutive day in the Pulivendula constituency of Kadapa district on Thursday as Telugu Desam Party (TDP) in-charge Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy, popularly known as ‘B.Tech Ravi’, staged a two-hour demonstration at the Pulivendula police station.

Accompanied by Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) Bhumireddy Ramagopal Reddy and two individuals allegedly injured in rival attacks, Mr. Ravi staged a sit-in in front of the station demanding a thorough investigation into a recent spate of political violence.

The protest was triggered by violent incidents reported in Agudur (Chakrayapet mandal) and Malyala (Thondur mandal), where several TDP workers and their properties – including those belonging to Simhadripuram Market Committee Chairman Bandi Ramasubba Reddy – were targeted.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Ravi visited the sites where the two-wheelers of TDP candidates were reportedly set ablaze to inspect the burnt remains.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ravi accused the police of inaction. “While individuals booked under Section 307 in firing cases are roaming freely on the streets, the police are turning a blind eye,” he alleged. “Despite video evidence showing these accused individuals moving alongside MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy, the department has taken no action.”
He further charged YSRCP leaders with driving tractors menacingly around nomination centres to intimidate voters and attempting to run them over TDP cadres.

Deputy Inspector-General of Police (Kurnool range) Koya Praveen, who had previously visited Pulivendula during the municipal elections to assure the safety of candidates and voters, intervened and offered to look into Mr. Ravi’s complaints once the nomination phase concludes.

Hitting back at the protest, Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy dismissed the sit-in outside the police station as “a big drama” and advised the TDP leader to refrain from what he termed “cheap politics”. In a counter-allegation, Mr. Avinash Reddy accused the TDP leadership of orchestrating attacks on YSRCP cadres by misusing official machinery, claiming that Mr. Ravi was now attempting to distort the facts to garner public sympathy.

Tense moments prevailed for the third consecutive day in the Pulivendula constituency of Kadapa district on Thursday as Telugu Desam Party (TDP) in-charge Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy, popularly known as ‘B.Tech Ravi’, staged a two-hour demonstration at the Pulivendula police station.

Accompanied by Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) Bhumireddy Ramagopal Reddy and two individuals allegedly injured in rival attacks, Mr. Ravi staged a sit-in in front of the station demanding a thorough investigation into a recent spate of political violence.

The protest was triggered by violent incidents reported in Agudur (Chakrayapet mandal) and Malyala (Thondur mandal), where several TDP workers and their properties – including those belonging to Simhadripuram Market Committee Chairman Bandi Ramasubba Reddy – were targeted.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Ravi visited the sites where the two-wheelers of TDP candidates were reportedly set ablaze to inspect the burnt remains.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ravi accused the police of inaction. “While individuals booked under Section 307 in firing cases are roaming freely on the streets, the police are turning a blind eye,” he alleged. “Despite video evidence showing these accused individuals moving alongside MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy, the department has taken no action.”

He further charged YSRCP leaders with driving tractors menacingly around nomination centres to intimidate voters and attempting to run them over TDP cadres.

Deputy Inspector-General of Police (Kurnool range) Koya Praveen, who had previously visited Pulivendula during the municipal elections to assure the safety of candidates and voters, intervened and offered to look into Mr. Ravi’s complaints once the nomination phase concludes.

Hitting back at the protest, Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy dismissed the sit-in outside the police station as “a big drama” and advised the TDP leader to refrain from what he termed “cheap politics”. In a counter-allegation, Mr. Avinash Reddy accused the TDP leadership of orchestrating attacks on YSRCP cadres by misusing official machinery, claiming that Mr. Ravi was now attempting to distort the facts to garner public sympathy.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Siddipet Govt medical college to be named after late Congress stalwart Madan Mohan
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy launched the Indiramma Family Insurance scheme in Siddipet on Thursday, which provides ₹5 lakh insurance cover to every family in State.

Addressing a public meeting with an impressive gathering, Mr. Reddy expressed the confidence that the Congress will retain power in the 2028 elections, given the introduction of new welfare schemes, while continuing the schemes of the earlier governments.

In a sharp attack on BRS MLA T Harish Rao, who represents the Siddipet constituency, and also the BRS chief K Chandrasekhar Rao, he challenged them to a debate in the Assembly on the Krishna and Godavari waters as the BRS was accusing him of failing the State in getting the rightful share.

Mr. Reddy claimed the BRS was targeting him as he was exposing the scams of the KCR family and the misgovernance of BRS. “I will continue to expose the wealth amassed by the KCR family, looting the State and compromising Telangana interests,” he said.

He made serious allegations against Mr. Harish Rao and asked him why he was denied the Irrigation Ministry by Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao in the second term. “Is it because he made huge money that made Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao angry,” he wondered.

The Chief Minister accused Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao of suppressing all those who sacrificed for Telangana while making thousands of crores. “Where are the leaders who sailed with Mr. KCR and Mr. Harish Rao during the Telangana movement,” he asked. Solipeta Ramalinga Reddy, T. Jagga Reddy and Cheruku Muthyam Reddy families are in debts while Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao’s family has become rich, he said.

He claimed that respected Congress leader Madanmohan, the political guru of Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao too was backstabbed. But the Congress would ensure his legacy in Siddipet naming the Government Medical college after Mr. Madan Mohan, the CM announced.

Stating that Siddipet would be wrested from the BRS in the next elections, he said TPCC president Mahesh Goud would ensure Siddipet MLA would be inducted in the Cabinet as the Congress was bound to win.
Mr. Reddy also claimed that Mr. Harish Rao was in talks with the BJP and asked him to vow on ‘Ellamma Talli’ who is revered by the Siddipet people.

On the Congress welfare schemes, he said one crore sarees would be distributed from November 26, and 8 lakh Indiramma houses would be constructed. Government has waived farm loans of up to ₹2 lakh, free rice through ration cards for the poor, ₹ 36,000 crore already distributed under the ‘Rythu Bharosa’ apart from free travel to women in the RTC buses, he said.

articles.title: Anthropic raises $81 billion in IPO amid AI market volatility
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Claude maker priced its shares at $83 apiece, implying an equity valuation of about $1.03 trillion based on outstanding shares, with trading scheduled to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19

Anthropic, the maker of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot Claude, has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 a share, valuing the offering at approximately $81.34 billion, according to an announcement by the company on November 18.

The company said its shares were expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT. The offering is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary closing conditions.

According to Anthropic’s announcement, the offering comprises 980 million shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 956.35 million shares are being sold by the company and 23.65 million by existing shareholders. Anthropic said it would not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling shareholders.

At the IPO price of $83 a share, the company’s portion of the offering is valued at approximately $79.38 billion, while the shares sold by existing shareholders are valued at approximately $1.96 billion. These figures are before underwriting discounts and expenses.
At $83 a share, Anthropic’s overall equity value works out to approximately $1.03 trillion, based on the total number of shares outstanding after the IPO.
Anthropic has also given the banks (underwriters) managing the IPO the option to purchase an additional 147 million shares within 30 days, potentially increasing the size of the offering.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters for the IPO, with JPMorgan, Citigroup, Barclays and other investment banks also participating, according to the SEC filing.
The IPO comes amid growing investor concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and whether technology companies can generate sufficient returns from their infrastructure spending.
On November 5, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5%, wiping out trillions of dollars in market value, while NVIDIA shares declined 9% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 12%.

Earlier, on October 29, Alphabet shares plunged 12.6%, wiping out approximately $500 billion in market value after its quarterly results raised concerns over its advertising business and the cash-flow impact of rising AI investments. The sell-off reflected broader concerns over the valuations of AI-linked companies and the returns from their heavy spending on data centres and computing infrastructure.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court, Maharashtra government decides to withdraw petition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe had challenged FSSAI over the constitutional validity of a few regulations. The petition had challenged the creation of a few posts by the Centre, claiming it was against the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court over a jurisdiction dispute, the Maharashtra government has taken a call to withdraw its petition, which had accused the Central government of usurping its power and creating new rules in a ‘clandestine manner’.

On September 3, 2026, Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration had filed a petition against FSSAI, challenging the constitutional validity of a few regulations. It had claimed that these regulations had led to the creation of ‘a parallel structure’ which ‘encroached upon the powers and duties of the State Commissioner of Food Safety and his officers.’ On October 29, the government directed officials to withdraw this petition, which had caused a stir as it led to a tussle between the Centre and the State, both governed by the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Political & National Report: Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court, Maharashtra government decides to withdraw petition. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Emerging radicalisation hotspots now under purview of Multi-Agency Centre: Amit Shah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union Home Minister calls on anti-terrorism squads of every State to strengthen their cyber-expert units

The Multi-Agency Centre (MAC), a centralised intelligence-sharing platform, now tracks cybersecurity, narcotics, organised crime networks, and emerging radicalisation hotspots, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The MAC, which also acts as a common counter-terrorism grid and functions under the Intelligence Bureau (IB), was conceptualised in 2001, in the aftermath of the Kargil war, but became fully operational in 2009.
In 2025, the MAC network was revamped to connect all police districts in the country through a secure network. Mr. Shah said that the functioning of the MAC has been reorganised.
He said that the anti-terrorism squads (ATS) of every State needed to strengthen their cyber-expert units as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes.

He made the remarks while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day counter-terrorism conference organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in New Delhi. On the occasion, he released the publication, Fail-Safe Investigation, brought out by the NIA. He also laid the foundation stone for the NIA’s office complex in Chandigarh and inaugurated the NIA’s residential complex at Maidangarhi in Delhi. In addition, the Union Home Minister e-launched the NIA’s ‘Pushti’ portal and conferred decorations on seven officers and personnel of the agency.

Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Intelligence Bureau Director Mahesh Dixit, Special Secretary (Internal Security) in the Ministry of Home Affairs, Anand Swarup, and NIA Director General Rakesh Aggarwal were present at the event.

Mr. Shah said that India has been confronting terrorism for a long time, and noted that while the police forces of different States had made various kinds of efforts, a lack of coordinated action was clearly visible. Over time, during the tenures of successive governments, gradual efforts were made to overcome these shortcomings, he said.

“Today, we can say with satisfaction that in this vast country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya — we are putting in place a system under which a uniform strategy to combat terrorism will operate right down to the level of every police station,” the Home Minister said.

He said that with the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Latif Bhat, Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists, adding that this situation has come about after 35 years. He also said that more than 40 modules of the Shahzad Bhatti network, which has been declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), have been neutralised across the country.

Mr. Shah said that the hallmark of a successful agency is apprehending terrorists and putting them behind bars before they can carry out their plans. He said the police in every State should analyse this model and implement it in their respective areas.

articles.title: Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court judge says a woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies

Justice B.V. Nagarathna, one of the senior most judges of the Supreme Court and in line to be the first woman Chief Justice of India, has said that the mere existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society.

“A woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies,” Justice Nagarathna said at the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College in the University of Oxford on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).
Only the practice of substantive equality could take care of these differences among women hailing from and living through diverse life experiences, the judge said.

Justice Nagarathna said a judgment cannot, by itself, guarantee that every workplace becomes safe, every girl receives education, every woman obtains her lawful inheritance, or every victim of domestic violence secures timely protection.
Likewise, legislation cannot achieve its full purpose if remedies were inaccessible, public authorities failed to act, or social attitudes prevent women from asserting their rights.

The judge said the enactment of Constitutional amendments which give women one-third of the seats in Parliament and the State legislatures was proof to show that women should participate in decision-making and not be content with just a formal right to vote.

“These developments reflect an important insight: where historical exclusion has shaped the composition of institutions, formal equality alone may not be sufficient to secure meaningful representation,” Justice Nagarathna pointed out.
Justice Nagarathna said that the progress of Indian women’s rights cannot be measured by the number of discriminatory provisions struck down or the enactment of a few beneficial laws.

The judge said recognition of violence against women as a violation of constitutional rights has not really translated in the real world to women seeking the protection of law without fear of stigma, retaliation or economic insecurity.

On the question of equality, Justice Nagarathna raised the fundamental problem of women being made to bear the “disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work which continues to determine women’s choices”.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: Landfall process begins
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours

The land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts early on Friday, says the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

articles.title: Removal proceedings against me infructuous after resignation: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha Secretariat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a letter circulated among MPs on November 19, Justice Varma stated that the proceedings directed toward his removal did not survive his resignation

Justice Yashwant Varma has contended that proceedings for his removal as a High Court judge became infructuous following his resignation and cannot be continued, saying any attempt to remove him from office would be without constitutional foundation.
In a letter dated September 10 to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh, he responded to the report of the inquiry committee constituted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.
Mr. Varma wrote that the proceedings directed towards his removal did not survive his resignation.

He reiterated that he was innocent of the allegations against him, including the suggestion that he possessed ill-gotten funds, and asserted that his resignation should not be construed as an acknowledgement or admission of any allegation or finding.
The letter was circulated among MPs on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
The three-member inquiry committee, in its report tabled in Parliament on August 12, had found all three charges against Justice Varma proved .

The charges related to his failure to explain the presence, source or ownership of cash found at his official residence, failure to secure and preserve material evidence leading to the unexplained disappearance of the currency, and evasive and unsatisfactory explanations during the inquiry.

articles.title: Mahua Moitra alleges attack on her convoy by BJP supporters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP leaders said the alleged attack was Ms. Moitra’s attempt to gain attention and conduct self-promotion through social media live videos

Mamata All India Trinamool Congress lawmaker Mahua Moitra on Thursday (November 19, 2026) alleged that Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members attacked her convoy when she was visiting her constituency — Krishnanagar — in Nadia district. She also accused the West Bengal police of inaction.

It is not the first time that the MP has been attacked since the BJP came to power in the State. “I have been attacked by the mob, with police waiting. My car was physically lifted. I have seen the same BJP member [I recognise his face] with flags,” Ms. Moitra said in a video statement after her car was attacked and vandalised.
She asked the Supreme Court, the Calcutta High Court, and the police to take note of the incident.

The Mamata loyalist also shared videos of BJP flags being carried by the mob that allegedly attacked her car and threw eggs at the windscreen. Ms. Moitra alleged that instead of rescuing her and neutralising the mob, the police personnel tried to stop her from attending her scheduled event in the area.
Meanwhile, Mamata's Trinamool general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and a Lok Sabha MP raised questions about the attack.

“Will the Calcutta High Court initiate contempt proceedings against the State Government and the Home Department for defying its orders, or does contempt of court apply only to the Opposition while those in power and their BJP allies enjoy special immunity?” Mr Banerjee asked.
West Bengal Industries Minister Tapas Roy said that without such incidents, Ms. Moitra does not get a chance to “go Live on Facebook”.

“She (Mahua Moitra) wants self-promotion. Now she does not have any other way of promotion, so these incidents are the only way for her to get some attention. If she wants, she can inform the court about any such incident,” Mr. Roy said.
On September 16, Ms. Moitra alleged that BJP workers pelted eggs on her during a visit to her Krishnanagar constituency in West Bengal’s Nadia.

All three major U.S. stock indexes ended the session ⁠sharply lower, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its fifth straight session of losses.
The S&P 500 was on course to post its steepest weekly loss since April 2025.

Anthropic’s debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced ‌on late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. “The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager ⁠at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri.
Even so, Ellerbroek’s enthusiasm for ‌the AI trade has waned.

“My beliefs about the growth in data centre capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two,” he added. “Nvidia’s crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact. Data centres are ‌going to be more expensive to build and they’re going to be built more ​slowly.”
Advanced Micro Devices shares tumbled after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.
Most chipmakers were ⁠lower, including Micron and Broadcom, among others.
Nvidia marked its sixth straight session of losses after the chipmaker’s upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

articles.title: The Rohingya question: International solidarity, accountability and the missing road home
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home?

The Rohingya question has returned to the centre of international attention following the landmark judgment delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on November 19, 2026. Yet, for more than a million Rohingya living outside Myanmar, legal recognition is only one part of a much larger struggle. articles.title: Draft of COP31 cover text drops references to fossil fuel phase-out, net zero dates
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated

The latest iteration of the COP 31 draft cover text has eliminated references to fossil fuel phase-out and net-zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries. This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

The COP31 Presidency’s revised draft cover decision, dated November 19, has 80 paragraphs, down from 144 in the November 16 version. The summit officially ends on November 20, though negotiations frequently overshoot into the weekend.

A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, scaling up the use of carbon capture utilisation technologies and making early warning systems universal by 2027, continue to find mention in the text. A broad commitment to triple adaptation finance also remains.

“ The draft cover text weaves the 35% electricity in final energy consumption by 2035, alongside tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling the rate of energy efficiency improvement by 2030, ” Ajay Mathur, India’s lead negotiator at Paris COP and former DG, International Solar Alliance, said in a statement. The electricity use in India went up by 13% in 2025 due to the Hormuz crisis alone. It will be an ambitious goal for India to achieve 35% electrification by 2035, but due to the increasing amount of renewable energy in the Indian energy mix, we will be near the 32-34% mark by 2035. ”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS) in a statement. “Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.
• Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.
Editorial Context: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. fullParagraphs: The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070

Islam is projected to be the world's largest religion by 2035, surpassing Christianity, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Centre on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Pew said if current trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under three billion Christians worldwide by 2070.
The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070.

But the rest of the world's population -- all non-Hindus -- will grow at an even faster rate. As a result, Hindus will shrink slightly as a share of the global population, falling from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070.
The world's total population is projected to increase by 29% between 2020 and 2070, with Christians growing by 30% and Muslims by 80%.
"The largest source of new members of major religions is not adults who convert to the faith, but babies who are born into the group," the Pew projections found.

During 2020-2025, the fertility rate for Muslims was 3.1 children per woman, followed by the rate for Christians at 2.5, Pew said. The average fertility rate for all other women was 1.6, below the 2.1 level considered necessary for each generation to replace itself.
If current demographic trends continue, the number of Hindus in India will increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070.

While India's overall fertility rate has fallen rapidly in recent decades, Muslims in India still have more children per woman than Hindus do, the Pew Research found. As per the Pew projections, Hindus comprise 79.4% of India's religious composition in 2020 and the number is set to slide to 75.8% by 2070.

Muslims comprise 15.2% of India's religious composition in 2020, and that share is set to rise to 19.6% by 2070. Outside India, much of the projected growth among Hindus will come from Pakistan (over five million) and the United States (over four million).
According to the Pew projections, the U.S. will have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Nepal and India will remain the only two countries with a Hindu majority.

articles.title: Kochi Corporation spends over ₹4 crore a year on nearly 2,000 defunct public taps
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Each public tap costs the Corporation ₹21,838 a year, irrespective of whether it is functional, taking the total annual expenditure to ₹11.70 crore

Nearly 2,000 of the 5,358 public taps identified in the city remain dysfunctional, for which the Kochi Corporation continues to pay the Kerala Water Authority (KWA) over ₹4 crore annually, resulting in a drain on the resources of the cash-strapped civic body.

A recent survey conducted by the Corporation through its overseers, in consultation with division councillors, found that 3,303 public taps were functional, while 1,995 were non-functional across the city. Each public tap costs the Corporation ₹21,838 a year, irrespective of whether it is functional, taking the total annual expenditure to ₹11.70 crore.

According to a letter issued by the KWA on November 6, 2025, there were 5,444 public taps within the city limits. The latest survey shows a marginal decline of 86 taps. Until the previous government completely wrote off the water charge arrears, around ₹5 crore used to be deducted annually from the Corporation’s Plan fund towards the dues.

Mayor V.K. Minimol said that despite free water connections provided under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation, several divisions still had more than 50 and even 100 public taps. articles.title: Hyderabad explores 35-km personal rapid transit network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The proposal is under active consideration, with the first phase envisaged between Kukatpally and Knowledge City via Raidurgam and Biodiversity Park
With traffic congestion worsening as the city expands, Hyderabad is exploring a 35-km Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS) to improve connectivity along key corridors.

The proposal is under active consideration, with the first phase envisaged between Kukatpally and Knowledge City via Raidurgam and Biodiversity Park. The proposed stretch would have 64 stations. Officials made a presentation on the plan to Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju at a meeting here on Wednesday.

The presentation followed directions from the Chief Secretary to prepare an action plan after Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy suggested exploring PRTS as an alternative mode of transport to ease congestion along important corridors. Mr. Jaju called for a comprehensive strategy to address the growing traffic challenges arising from the city’s rapid expansion.
Hyderabad Metro Rail officials, who studied the feasibility of PRTS and other transport systems, projected daily commuter demand at 3.94 lakh by 2030, 7.96 lakh by 2040 and 10 lakh by 2050.

Mr. Jaju asked officials to identify potential PRTS corridors based on traffic density and ensure optimum use of existing transport systems. He also stressed that the proposed network should be developed at minimum cost. Hyderabad Metro Rail Limited officials were directed to expedite consultations with technical experts and potential project partners.

He also called for effective coordination among departments, including Municipal Administration, Energy, South Central Railway and HYDRAA, to ensure integrated traffic planning that takes the city’s future needs into account.

articles.title: Census 2027: ‘Other’ religions list made predictive text, over 200 entries from earlier list dropped
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This comes days after The Hindu reported that at least 287 entries such as ISKCON, Gorak Nath, Sanatan, Vedic Dharm, Ramdev etc. had been listed in a drop-down menu for “Other” religions on the portal and then removed
The 2027 Census self-enumeration portal is now showing a total of 76 entries under the “Other” religions that now appear as predictive text suggestions and not as a drop-down menu.

This comes days after The Hindu reported that at least 287 entries such as ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Gorak Nath , Sanatan, Vedic Dharm, Ramdev etc., had been listed in a drop-down menu for “Other” religions on the portal and then removed.

An examination of the new list of available “Other” religions showed that the Union government removed over 200 entries that were previously listed under the same category on Monday (November 16, 2026), the day the portal went live for four poll-bound States — Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand.

The deletions include entries such as Satguru, Ramdev, ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Gorak Nath, Sanatan, Bishnoi, Vaishnaw, Shia, Sunni, and many others that were either classified in earlier Censuses as sects within the six major religions (Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Jain, Buddhist) or seemed to be new entries not recorded in previous Censuses at all.

Out of the 76 predictive text suggestions that now remain on the portal, nearly all appear to have already been recorded and tabulated based on the 2011 Census data on what people chose to write their faith as under the “Other” column. A majority of these entries include the religions and faiths of Scheduled Tribe communities across the country — such as Sarna, Doni Polo, Tana Bhagat, Birsa, Garo, Munda, Oraon, Santal, etc.

Apart from these, five entries in this new list of suggestive “other” religions do not feature in the 2011 or 2001 Census tables for “Other religions and persuasions”. These include “Adibasi dharma”, “Bura Deo”, “Karupa”, “Tingkao Rangong”, and “Tingwang Hingde”.

Soon after The Hindu reported the presence of a drop-down for “other” religions and its quick removal, Opposition leaders and OBC associations alike questioned the integrity of the way the 2027 Census was being conducted, with many of them questioning how the government was comfortable introducing a drop-down for religions but not for caste. Experts had also questioned the introduction of previously unrecorded entries in this drop-down, saying there would be nothing to compare these with.
Interestingly, a section of general category communities in north India reacted to the presence of 287 “other” religions by saying this was an alleged attempt to “divide Hindus”.

On Monday (November 16, 2026), when the self-enumeration portal went live, the initial list of 287 entries for “Other” religions appeared as a drop-down menu from which respondents could select one in addition to writing in whatever they wanted. Within hours of The Hindu sending a query to the Union Home Ministry, this drop-down menu was removed, and a representative of the Office of the RGI and the Census Commissioner said it would be “incorrect” to say these entries were shown as “other” religions.

However, a government official had told The Hindu at the time that this list was part of “predictive text entries” to help reduce variations and mistakes in spellings. But officials did not clarify how previously unrecorded entries such as ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Ramdev, Gorak Nath, etc. had appeared on this list either.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 19 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Census 2027: ‘Other’ religions list made predictive text, over 200 entries from earlier list dropped

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

This comes days after The Hindu reported that at least 287 entries such as ISKCON, Gorak Nath, Sanatan, Vedic Dharm, Ramdev etc. had been listed in a drop-down menu for “Other” religions on the portal and then removed

The 2027 Census self-enumeration portal is now showing a total of 76 entries under the “Other” religions that now appear as predictive text suggestions and not as a drop-down menu.

This comes days after The Hindu reported that at least 287 entries such as ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Gorak Nath , Sanatan, Vedic Dharm, Ramdev etc., had been listed in a drop-down menu for “Other” religions on the portal and then removed.

An examination of the new list of available “Other” religions showed that the Union government removed over 200 entries that were previously listed under the same category on Monday (November 16, 2026), the day the portal went live for four poll-bound States — Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand.

The deletions include entries such as Satguru, Ramdev, ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Gorak Nath, Sanatan, Bishnoi, Vaishnaw, Shia, Sunni, and many others that were either classified in earlier Censuses as sects within the six major religions (Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Jain, Buddhist) or seemed to be new entries not recorded in previous Censuses at all.

Out of the 76 predictive text suggestions that now remain on the portal, nearly all appear to have already been recorded and tabulated based on the 2011 Census data on what people chose to write their faith as under the “Other” column. A majority of these entries include the religions and faiths of Scheduled Tribe communities across the country — such as Sarna, Doni Polo, Tana Bhagat, Birsa, Garo, Munda, Oraon, Santal, etc.

Apart from these, five entries in this new list of suggestive “other” religions do not feature in the 2011 or 2001 Census tables for “Other religions and persuasions”. These include “Adibasi dharma”, “Bura Deo”, “Karupa”, “Tingkao Rangong”, and “Tingwang Hingde”.

Soon after The Hindu reported the presence of a drop-down for “other” religions and its quick removal, Opposition leaders and OBC associations alike questioned the integrity of the way the 2027 Census was being conducted, with many of them questioning how the government was comfortable introducing a drop-down for religions but not for caste. Experts had also questioned the introduction of previously unrecorded entries in this drop-down, saying there would be nothing to compare these with.

Interestingly, a section of general category communities in north India reacted to the presence of 287 “other” religions by saying this was an alleged attempt to “divide Hindus”.

On Monday (November 16, 2026), when the self-enumeration portal went live, the initial list of 287 entries for “Other” religions appeared as a drop-down menu from which respondents could select one in addition to writing in whatever they wanted. Within hours of The Hindu sending a query to the Union Home Ministry, this drop-down menu was removed, and a representative of the Office of the RGI and the Census Commissioner said it would be “incorrect” to say these entries were shown as “other” religions.

However, a government official had told The Hindu at the time that this list was part of “predictive text entries” to help reduce variations and mistakes in spellings. But officials did not clarify how previously unrecorded entries such as ISKCON, Ramkrishna Paramhans, Ramdev, Gorak Nath, etc. had appeared on this list either.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: However, a government official had told The Hindu at the time that this list was part of “predictive text entries” to help reduce variations and mistakes in spellings. articles.title: Congress targets Modi government over inflation, seeks white paper on rising prices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kharge says common person’s plate is getting smaller, pockets getting emptier, and making ends meet is getting harder

Accusing the Narendra Modi government of failing to control inflation, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) said the country's progress should be measured by the food on people’s plates and the money in their pockets, not the length of the Prime Minister's speeches.
His colleague and the party's communication chief, Jairam Ramesh, asked the Prime Minister to come out with a white paper on inflation.

“Modi ji promised to bring down inflation, but today the situation is such that the common person’s plate is getting smaller, their pockets are getting emptier, and making ends meet is becoming increasingly difficult,” Mr. Kharge said in a post on X.

Pointing to the rise in prices of essential commodities over the past 12 years, he said the cost of wheat flour had risen from ₹21 to ₹69 per kg, pigeon peas from ₹75 to ₹180, mustard oil from ₹102 to ₹263, and milk from ₹36 to ₹85.

“The measure of the country’s progress is not the length of your speeches, but the food on the common person’s plate and the money left in their pocket. How much longer will people keep paying the price for your economic mismanagement?” the Congress president asked.
Mr. Ramesh flagged the impact of rising prices on household budgets, citing reports of impending price increases in consumer goods ranging from smartphones and televisions to biscuits and salt.
He said companies were either raising prices or reducing the quantity in packets, leaving consumers with less for their money.

Retail inflation had reached 6.09% in October, with food inflation at 8.94%, while wholesale inflation stood at 12.29%, Mr. Ramesh said, adding that the latter was the highest under the current Wholesale Price Index series. He said that inflationary pressures were now affecting both household spending and production costs.

Citing a survey, he said 61% of households had seen their monthly expenditure on essential items rise by more than 20% over the past year, while 74% had been forced to cut down on non-essential spending.
He also flagged the possibility of higher equated monthly instalments following the Reserve Bank of India’s October increase in the repo rate.

articles.title: BJP turns to Mathura temple issue amid cadre unease, allies’ pressure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Political observers say the renewed focus on Krishna Janmabhoomi serves as a “smokescreen” to mask simmering discontent among the party cadre over the UGC’s equity rules, SIR drive and seat sharing with alliance partners

Days after Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav made his ‘Dumdar Dalit’ outreach in Agra, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) responded on November 16 with ‘Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De’ and ‘Abki Baari Baanke Bihari’.

It was senior BJP leader and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya who spelt out to reporters, during the party’s two-day conclave in Mathura earlier this week, that constructing a grand temple at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura would be at the centre of their campaign for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. The ruling party signalled that it would counter the SP’s ‘PDA’ [‘Pichhde’ (backward classes), Dalits and ‘Alpsankhyak’ (minorities)] card with the mantra of cultural nationalism, supplementing it with the ‘double-engine’ government’s “success stories” on the development and law and order fronts.
