articles.title: U.S., Venezuela sign deal to re-establish military ties: Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Defence Secretary said that following the January capture of Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking in Venezuela, said the two countries have signed an agreement to re-establish military ties, from training to intelligence sharing.

Mr. Hegseth said that following the January capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner.”
Mr. Hegseth also praised the “close cooperation” with interim President Delcy Rodriguez that allowed officials “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all.”
The Pentagon did not immediately offer further details on the new partnership.

Ms. Rodríguez separately lauded the opportunity to strengthen the military partnership. “I hope that this technical-military cooperation … can be brought to its highest possible level so that ... we may address common threats,” she said.
Mr. Hegseth’s visit underscores efforts by President Donald Trump’s administration to deepen its influence in the South American country since U.S. forces ousted Maduro in January.

Mr. Hegseth is the latest member of Mr. Trump’s Cabinet to travel to Venezuela following visits this year by the Interior and Energy secretaries, who have focused on efforts to tap its oil reserves and critical minerals. Mr. Trump said in August that Mr. Hegseth helped broker a sweeping deal for the U.S. to take control of some Venezuelan oil reserves.
The head of U.S. military operations in Latin America, Gen. Francis Donovan of U.S. Southern Command, also has met interim authorities in Venezuela at least twice this year.

The U.S. military has been expanding its attention on the region since Mr. Trump returned to the White House last year, with the Republican president promising to focus more on the Western Hemisphere and battle Latin American drug cartels.

To try to stem the flow of narcotics into the U.S. and the scourge of fatal overdoses, American forces have been attacking what the Trump administration says are boats smuggling drugs in the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean. At least 240 people have been killed since the administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” in September 2025, although U.S. officials have released little evidence publicly to support claims the vessels were carrying drugs.

articles.title: Panjab University improves its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition

Chandigarh-based Panjab University (PU) has improved its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research, climbing 24 places to secure the joint 150th position in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027. The University’s overall score has increased to 55.0 from 52.8 in 2026 and 48.6 in 2025.

In a statement on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Vice-Chancellor Meenakshi Goyal said, “This improvement in Panjab University’s global standing reflects our continued commitment to strengthening interdisciplinary research and academic collaboration. It is the outcome of the collective efforts of our faculty, researchers, students, and staff. We will continue to build an enabling research ecosystem that encourages collaboration across disciplines, supports innovation, and addresses complex societal challenges aimed at Viksit Bharat through knowledge and research.”

The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition. A total of 565 Asian institutions were ranked, up from 478 last year.

The Interdisciplinary Science Rankings assess universities’ contributions and commitment to research that brings together knowledge and methods from different academic disciplines to address complex challenges. The rankings cover collaborations involving multiple scientific disciplines as well as research combining scientific disciplines with areas such as the social sciences, education, psychology, law, economics, and clinical and health studies.

articles.title: COVID-19 lessons should inform response to air pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Tackling air pollution already attracts considerable expenditure, but allocations do not consistently reflect the greatest health risks

There is an uncanny similarity between Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic, and air pollution. During the pandemic, the virus entered our bodies through the air we breathed; harmful particulate matter and toxic gases enter through the same respiratory route. Additionally, both damage multiple organs, including the lungs, heart and brain. Yet, while COVID-19 prompted an unprecedented emergency national response, air pollution continues to be treated largely as a seasonal inconvenience.

The harmful effects of air pollution are well-established. An adult takes approximately 20,000–25,000 breaths daily, meaning that even a relatively miniscule worsening of air quality can have substantial health consequences over time. This alone should make improving the quality of air an urgent public health priority.

Science, Space & Environment Report: COVID-19 lessons should inform response to air pollution. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Climate promises need to become praxis
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The world does not lack climate declarations. They simply do not have the speed, resources, and cooperation required to make them a reality
Climate change is no longer a distant concern. The question is no longer whether countries should act, but whether they can turn promises into praxis quickly and fairly.

During COP29 in Baku in 2024, countries agreed to provide up to $300 billion dollars per year to developing countries by 2035. They also called for the mobilisation of $1.3 trillion a year from public and private sectors. While these commitments acknowledge that there is a need for vulnerable countries to receive more support, the true test is whether the funds are delivered on time to countries at affordable prices and in a usable format.

articles.title: A regulatory fix for India’s campuses
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Ministry must act without delay and issue a statutory notification, consistent with the court’s judgment, for eligible educational campuses

India’s education infrastructure has always been the strongest foundation of its growth and development. However, recent Supreme Court judgments have reaffirmed that educational buildings exceeding 20,000 square metres require prior Environmental Clearance (EC) under the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006. Institutions that have already constructed such buildings without obtaining clearance are now left without any procedure to secure it, creating a serious obstacle. The issue has developed because of two major regulatory changes.

Before the EIA Notification, 2006, there was no built-up-area-based EC requirement for educational institutions. The Notification brought large construction projects, including educational campuses, within the prior EC framework. In December 2014, the Union government exempted schools, colleges and institutional hostels from EC, subject to environmental management conditions. The Kerala High Court quashed this exemption in March 2024. The government introduced a fresh exemption in January 2025, but Vanashakti challenged it before the Supreme Court. After staying its operation, the court cancelled the exemption in August 2025. Consequently, large educational buildings again became subject to prior EC requirements.
Science, Space & Environment Report: A regulatory fix for India’s campuses. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: ‘Development has meaning only when the poor have food on their plates’, says CM D.K. Shivakumar as he inaugurates 16 Indira Canteens
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Shivakumar asked municipal bodies to ensure that the quality of food was maintained and called for CCTV cameras to be installed at the canteens, with footage monitored centrally.

“Does hunger have a caste or religion? Does it discriminate? Even the richest person, when hungry, does not look at someone’s caste or religion before eating,” Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as he digitally inaugurated 16 new Indira Canteens across urban local bodies in Karnataka on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

Saying that development had meaning only when there was food on a poor person’s plate, Mr. Shivakumar said the canteens were part of Indira Gandhi’s dream of poverty eradication. Recalling her slogan ‘Garibi Hatao’, he said she had worked towards ensuring that poor people had food and the means to earn their livelihood. “The canteens were being run in her name to carry forward that vision,” he said.

“Indira Canteens provide breakfast at ₹5 and meals at ₹10. They are intended to serve daily-wage workers, auto and taxi drivers, small traders and other poor people living in cities. The government plans to increase the number of canteens to over 380,” he said, adding that several outlets were yet to be completed and the pending work should be expedited.
People seen in front of Indira canteen near Askok Pillar at Jayanagar, in Bengaluru. File photo. | Photo Credit: MURALI KUMAR K

Mr. Shivakumar also spoke about how the idea of Indira Canteens came about. He said that during one of his visits to Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu, he had gone to an Amma Canteen and had breakfast for ₹5. The idli and pongal served there, and the quality of food available at such a low price, had impressed him. He later spoke to Siddaramaiah, who was then the Chief Minister, and other leaders about starting a similar initiative in Karnataka. The legislators supported the idea and suggested that it be named after Indira Gandhi.

He said the Congress had always stood for the poor and weaker sections and referred to the Right to Food Act brought in during the UPA government under former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, with Sonia Gandhi as the chairperson. He also recalled the mid-day meal programme introduced during S.M. Krishna’s tenure as Chief Minister and said the Siddaramaiah government had taken this approach forward through schemes such as Anna Bhagya and the five guarantees.
“Prices are soaring while incomes are falling. Our aim is not just to remove hunger, but to ensure that everyone has protection. The faces of those who work hard should always have a smile,” he said.

Mr. Shivakumar asked municipal bodies to ensure that the quality of food was maintained and called for CCTV cameras to be installed at the canteens, with footage monitored centrally. He said the system should help track how many people visited, how much food was prepared and how much was served.
An elderly man having a meal at the Indira Canteen in Benson Town, in Bengaluru on February 10, 2026. | Photo Credit: ALLEN EGENUSE J

He also said municipal officials should be assigned specific canteens and made to visit them regularly, eat there and check the quality of food and services. Contractors too should be held accountable. “There will be no compromise on quality,” he warned, adding that officials would be held responsible for lapses even if they were committed at the behest of elected representatives.

Mr. Shivakumar also spoke about how the idea of Indira Canteens came about. He said that during one of his visits to Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu, he had gone to an Amma Canteen and had breakfast for ₹5. The idli and pongal served there, and the quality of food available at such a low price, had impressed him. He later spoke to Siddaramaiah, who was then the Chief Minister, and other leaders about starting a similar initiative in Karnataka. The legislators supported the idea and suggested that it be named after Indira Gandhi.

He said the Congress had always stood for the poor and weaker sections and referred to the Right to Food Act brought in during the UPA government under former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, with Sonia Gandhi as the chairperson. He also recalled the mid-day meal programme introduced during S.M. Krishna’s tenure as Chief Minister and said the Siddaramaiah government had taken this approach forward through schemes such as Anna Bhagya and the five guarantees.

Mr. Shivakumar asked municipal bodies to ensure that the quality of food was maintained and called for CCTV cameras to be installed at the canteens, with footage monitored centrally. He said the system should help track how many people visited, how much food was prepared and how much was served.

articles.title: EPFO tells trustees there’s no legal route to recover ₹1,800 crore from Reliance Capital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: EPFO’s Central Board of Trustees will discuss the status of the outstanding default on the retirement fund’s holdings and review the annual performance of its portfolio managers at a meeting on Thursday

The alleged siphoning of the remaining ₹1,800 crore of salaried workers’ money that Reliance Capital Ltd (RCL) has defaulted on paying to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is part of the agenda of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) meeting, scheduled to be held here on Thursday (November 19, 2026). According to the agenda note, seen by The Hindu , the EPFO may not be able to claim any more of the principal amount or interest under any legal route.

Among the issues to be discussed in the meeting are the status of the outstanding default on the retirement fund’s holdings and the annual performance of its portfolio managers. CBT members will also discuss the material shared by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on alleged fraudulent transactions, diversion of funds, irregular lending, and other alleged irregularities by the RCL.

The EPFO invested ₹2,500 crore of workers’ money with the RCL in 2013 and 2014, and the latter defaulted on it and is alleged to have impaired the security available to debenture holders, including the EPFO. The EPFO’s admitted claim from the RCL was ₹3,308.67 crore, out of which ₹2,500 crore was the principal amount invested. The investment was scheduled to mature in 2023 and 2024.

The custodian of the RCL, Standard Chartered Bank, has reported the receipt of ₹1,492.45 crore, i.e., 59.70% of the principal amount. “Total amount invested but not received as on 19.03.2025 is ₹1,007.55 crore, and the amount of interest admitted in Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) but not received is ₹808.67 crore,” the agenda note for Thursday’s meeting said.

The agenda note, citing the legal opinion of EPFO’s lawyer, added that no further legal remedy exists for additional recovery in view of binding Supreme Court judgments, the resolution plan approved by the National Company Law Tribunal, and the full-and-final settlement nature of distributions received. “The EPFO may not be able to claim further principal or interest under any legal route,” the agenda note adds.

A spokesperson for businessman Anil Ambani had earlier said that Mr. Ambani served as a non-executive director/chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 to November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the board of directors of the company and appointed an administrator. “Mr. Ambani has denied any wrongdoing whatsoever and reserves all rights available to him in law,” the spokesperson had said.

The EPFO has told its trustees that the Central Bureau of Investigation has registered a case into the matter. The organisation has written to the ED on the issue and asked the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to refer the matter to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO).

“Considering the nature of the allegations and the financial loss suffered by EPFO, legal consultation was sought on the matter. Based on the legal opinion received, a reference was made to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for registration of FIR, investigation into the alleged fraudulent transactions, and for such appropriate action in accordance with the law,” says the agenda note circulated among members.

The meeting will also discuss the status of other defaulters, including the Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation (outstanding interest of about ₹85 crore), Richardson & Cruddas (a penal interest of about ₹5.36 crore), Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services Limited (a claim of ₹601.54 crore), and the Punjab State Industrial Development Corporation (₹1.10 crore interest in default).

The meeting will also review the performance of portfolio managers such as the UTI Asset Management Company Ltd, SBI Fund Management Ltd, and four asset management companies for Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) investments — UTI Asset Management Company Limited, SBI Funds Management Limited, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited, and Nippon India Life AMC. The evaluation report is prepared by M/s. CRISIL.

The EPFO invested ₹2,500 crore of workers’ money with the RCL in 2013 and 2014, and the latter defaulted on it and is alleged to have impaired the security available to debenture holders, including the EPFO. The EPFO’s admitted claim from the RCL was ₹3,308.67 crore, out of which ₹2,500 crore was the principal amount invested. The investment was scheduled to mature in 2023 and 2024.

The custodian of the RCL, Standard Chartered Bank, has reported the receipt of ₹1,492.45 crore, i.e., 59.70% of the principal amount. “Total amount invested but not received as on 19.03.2025 is ₹1,007.55 crore, and the amount of interest admitted in Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) but not received is ₹808.67 crore,” the agenda note for Thursday’s meeting said.

The agenda note, citing the legal opinion of EPFO’s lawyer, added that no further legal remedy exists for additional recovery in view of binding Supreme Court judgments, the resolution plan approved by the National Company Law Tribunal, and the full-and-final settlement nature of distributions received. “The EPFO may not be able to claim further principal or interest under any legal route,” the agenda note adds.

A spokesperson for businessman Anil Ambani had earlier said that Mr. Ambani served as a non-executive director/chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 to November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the board of directors of the company and appointed an administrator. “Mr. Ambani has denied any wrongdoing whatsoever and reserves all rights available to him in law,” the spokesperson had said.

The EPFO has told its trustees that the Central Bureau of Investigation has registered a case into the matter. The organisation has written to the ED on the issue and asked the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to refer the matter to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO).

“Considering the nature of the allegations and the financial loss suffered by EPFO, legal consultation was sought on the matter. Based on the legal opinion received, a reference was made to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for registration of FIR, investigation into the alleged fraudulent transactions, and for such appropriate action in accordance with the law,” says the agenda note circulated among members.

The meeting will also discuss the status of other defaulters, including the Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation (outstanding interest of about ₹85 crore), Richardson & Cruddas (a penal interest of about ₹5.36 crore), Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services Limited (a claim of ₹601.54 crore), and the Punjab State Industrial Development Corporation (₹1.10 crore interest in default).

The meeting will also review the performance of portfolio managers such as the UTI Asset Management Company Ltd, SBI Fund Management Ltd, and four asset management companies for Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) investments — UTI Asset Management Company Limited, SBI Funds Management Limited, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited, and Nippon India Life AMC. Mr. Modi highlighted achievements of his government in the last 12-13 years, and lauded efforts made by all sections of the society.

While the government has reduced the corporate tax, he asked if the industry has increased the strength of employees and raised their wages.
He also emphasised that a country progresses when it respects its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers, and not by hurling abuses day-in and day-out.
Taking a jibe at past regimes, Mr. Modi said the industry's experience with previous governments has been so bitter that he has to bear the consequences.

articles.title: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ heads for Odisha; over one lakh people evacuated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Odisha Government closes coastal tourist sites including Chilika Lake, Puri beaches, Bhitarakanika and Nandankanan Zoological Park

Odisha on Thursday (November 19, 2026) stepped up evacuation of people, positioning of disaster response forces and emptying of reservoirs in southern and coastal districts as the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ is expected cross the State’s coast, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon of November 20.

Office of Special Relief Commissioner said more than one lakh people, including close to 10,000 pregnant women, have been shifted to safer places. While Ganjam district under which Gopalpur lies alone has shifted over 50,000 people, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts have relocated 16,000 and 3000 people respectively.
Ghat roads (hill passes) such as Kalinga and Gajalbadi connecting Ganjam and Kandhamal districts have been barricaded, apprehending landslides.

“The Severe Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved northwards with the speed of 15 kmph during past six hours and lay centered about 420 km east-southeast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 400 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 490 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 550 km south of Puri (Odisha) and 590 km east-northeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu),” the India Meteorological Department announced in a bulletin.

The IMD bulletin said it is likely to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon of November 20, 2026, with maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph. Experts, however, said the windspeed could come down to 70 to 80 km per hour when the cyclone would cross the coast.
A red warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall has been issued for Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, Puri, Ganjam, Gajapati, and Kandhamal districts.
Gopalpur Port authorities have secured machineries and ships in view advancing cyclone after the government’s warning.

“Water resources department has started depleting reservoirs in districts to be affected by the cyclone. Engineers are continuously monitoring situation while technical teams have been deployed. Two gates of major dam and 23 gates of different medium irrigation dams are kept opened,” said Odisha Chief Secretary Anu Garg.
A man, identified Santosh Palaka (38), went missing when river water level in Sana Nadi rises in Gudari block of Rayagada district after water from Harabhangi dam was released.

In Ganjam district, the drainage division of Berhampur, had undertaken breach closure works at Bahana Nalla near Kalinga Bihar and Dura, Taptapani Nalla near Chanameri village, and Padmatola Nalla near Gudipadar village in Patrapur Block. These interventions were aimed at strengthening vulnerable drainage infrastructure and ensuring its preparedness ahead of the impending cyclone.

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi calls for continued dialogue with China to ease bilateral tensions
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday (November 19, 2026) called for continued dialogue and communication with China to ease bilateral tensions triggered by her remarks on Taiwan, saying Beijing is an "important neighbour" with which Tokyo has several outstanding issues.
Ms. Takaichi is in Shenzhen to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.

"China is an important neighbour, and between the two countries there are outstanding issues, and that is why it is important to continue communicating and having dialogue,” she told the media on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
When asked about her brief interaction with Mr. Xi, the Japanese PM said she thanked him for the invitation and congratulated him on successfully hosting the APEC summit.

Relations between Tokyo and Beijing have sharply deteriorated after Takaichi told parliament in November last year that a Chinese attack on Taiwan, a self-governed island claimed by China, could trigger a situation in which Japan's Self-Defence Forces might support US forces.
Her remarks infuriated China, prompting it to take a series of political and economic measures against Japan, including export restrictions on rare earths used in a wide range of high-tech products.
Asked about the controversy, Ms. Takaichi said Japan's four political documents governing its relations with China remained unchanged and continued to serve as the foundation of bilateral ties.

Tokyo will continue to advance a comprehensive strategic relationship of mutual benefit with Beijing while pursuing dialogue to protect their respective national interests and build constructive and stable ties, she said, according to the Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post.
Ms. Takaichi refrained from commenting on a hypothetical Taiwan contingency, saying Japan's position on Taiwan, as articulated in the 1972 Japan-China Joint Communique, remained unchanged.

articles.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting LIVE: Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge again as Trump says U.S., China want to help end war
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: China-U.S. relations 'stable and improved', Xi says; Trilateral summit to begin shortly on the sidelines of the ongoing APEC Summit

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.
The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

Fyodor Lukyanov, a pro-Kremlin foreign policy expert, noted that even as Moscow publicly rejects the Yalta analogy, it seems to believe the leaders could “reach agreements and make decisions that will determine global developments”.
Of the three nations, “it seems that only Russia really believes in the possibility of global control”, he told a recent roundtable.

Chatham House director Bronwen Maddox said in a commentary that “standing with Xi and Trump, Putin will look like one of the three main leaders of the world”, even though “Russia is no superpower” and its economy, overloaded with military spending, is dwindling.
She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

The meeting follows US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine held in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months. The negotiations produced few visible results as the parties stuck to their sharply divergent demands. -- AP
Trilateral Xi-Putin-Trump summit draws Yalta 1945 comparisons, highlighting postwar order shifts amid Ukraine tensions and multipolar world debates.

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday (November 19, 2026) told U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping that their three countries shared an “interest” in resolving the Ukraine war and a “responsibility” for global peace and security.

“Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Mr. Putin said in opening remarks at a landmark summit between the three leaders in Shenzhen.

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.

The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

Fyodor Lukyanov, a pro-Kremlin foreign policy expert, noted that even as Moscow publicly rejects the Yalta analogy, it seems to believe the leaders could “reach agreements and make decisions that will determine global developments”.

Of the three nations, “it seems that only Russia really believes in the possibility of global control”, he told a recent roundtable.

Chatham House director Bronwen Maddox said in a commentary that “standing with Xi and Trump, Putin will look like one of the three main leaders of the world”, even though “Russia is no superpower” and its economy, overloaded with military spending, is dwindling.

She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

The meeting follows US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine held in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months. The negotiations produced few visible results as the parties stuck to their sharply divergent demands. -- AP

articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests
India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik.
Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said.

Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests.

Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12.

Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added.

“The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar.

“The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said.
Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.

fullParagraphs: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮‍💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in India in September 2013, priced at around ₹3,000 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. But its second life here began after PUBG Mobile was banned in September 2020. Several of India’s biggest streamers, including Dynamo and MortaL, turned to other games, GTA V among them, and roleplay helped make it a mainstay of Indian livestreaming.

A roleplay server is a fan-run version of GTA V’s online world where players invent characters with names, jobs and backstories, from cab drivers and paramedics to cops and small-time crooks, and inhabit them for hours. Soulcity, launched by S8UL and Velocity Gaming in early 2023, became one of India’s biggest GTA V roleplay servers and helped create a new breed of gaming star. S8UL co-founder Lokesh Jain, better known as 8Bit Goldy, played a character called Rocket Singh on the server. The scene grew big enough for S8UL to sign creators such as Sunny Jha, aka Pitaji Playz, specifically for its GTA roleplay roster.

articles.title: GTA VI goes live: Inside Rockstar Games’ biggest video game yet
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: After a 13-year wait, GTA VI is finally here. Built on an estimated $1.5 billion, the game takes players into Leonida’s crime-filled world. Here’s a closer look

Putting an end to the long waiting period of over 13 years, the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI by Rockstar Games went live on Thursday (November 19, 2026) for millions of gamers across the globe, offering a gripping landscape of blazing action sequences and adventure-packed missions. The Rockstar Games’ biggest video game, widely reported to be the most expensive cultural product ever made of around $1.5 billion, has released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. The plot is set in Leonida (a Florida-inspired city), buzzing with traffic, crime and sun-drenched beaches, pairing spectacular visuals with the rise of two small-time criminals through the city’s underworld.

The central characters are a criminal couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose action-packed adventures punctuated by slow-motion effects and dramatic camera shifts is expected to the highlight of the videogame. Lucia has recently been released from prison, while Jason is a former soldier who became involved with drug runners in the Leonida Keys. When a criminal job goes wrong, the pair become entangled in a wider conspiracy.
Based on the latest reports, the videogame is not on the cards for the official release in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

As per the official site, over 4,700 employees cutting across a dozen studios of Rockstar studios, devoted more than eight years to build the latest instalment of GTA. The active production only began after the release of Rockstar’s previous game, Red Dead Redemption II, in 2018. Earlier slated for a late 2025 release , the game’s launch was postponed twice owing to a series of leaks in 2022 and the online release of stolen gameplay videos.

Developers immersed themselves in the region while building the game, driving through Miami, the Florida Keys and surrounding communities, flying over the Everglades and researching the area’s history and architecture.

In a bid to cater to the immersive gameplay experience, the videogame allows players to tune into more than 20 radio stations at home or in their vehicles, with music ranging from Simple Minds and Daft Punk to Van Halen. A fresh addition in the latest instalment is podcasts. Among the options is a true-crime-style series chronicling Vice City, the game’s main metropolis.

The videogame’s plot unfolds by building the relationship between Jason and Lucia, from a chance encounter during a police stop to a robbery gone wrong that lands Lucia in jail. Much of the adventure transpires through lengthy cinematic cut-scenes, allowing players to sit back and watch the story. Only later does the game open up and hand players control of Jason’s day-to-day life, a former soldier working for local gangsters, who is recovering drug packages dropped at sea, stealing cars and shaking down debtors.

The videogame’s release has sparked a wave of excitement among gamers for detailed attention to the graphics. In GTA VI, the hair sways in the wind, muscles flex beneath clothing and characters move with a naturalism. The fictional state of Leonida, Rockstar’s take on Florida, enables a larger-than-life experience to the gamers. This is enveloped by bustling city streets, neon-soaked nightlife and pristine beaches all feature in a vast 3D world that players can explore while scuba diving.

Further, the game’s map is learnt to be one of the biggest and busiest ever made in the GTA-series history. The latest addition allows the non-player characters go about their own lives, and the world seems to carry on whether the player is involved or not. A simple drive across town might involve a random police traffic stop, witnessing a car accident or stumbling across a robbery by the beach.

Additionally, players are likely to find cars heavier in the latest instalment of the video-game, relatably tough to manoeuvre with a responsibility to keep an eye on their fuel tanks. They also decide what stays in a car trunk and what comes along for the ride, juggle phone calls and messages, and use apps to identify targets or track potential scores.

📰 GTA VI goes live: Inside Rockstar Games’ biggest video game yet

After a 13-year wait, GTA VI is finally here. Built on an estimated $1.5 billion, the game takes players into Leonida’s crime-filled world. Here’s a closer look

Putting an end to the long waiting period of over 13 years, the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI by Rockstar Games went live on Thursday (November 19, 2026) for millions of gamers across the globe, offering a gripping landscape of blazing action sequences and adventure-packed missions. The Rockstar Games’ biggest video game, widely reported to be the most expensive cultural product ever made of around $1.5 billion, has released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. The plot is set in Leonida (a Florida-inspired city), buzzing with traffic, crime and sun-drenched beaches, pairing spectacular visuals with the rise of two small-time criminals through the city’s underworld.

The central characters are a criminal couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose action-packed adventures punctuated by slow-motion effects and dramatic camera shifts is expected to the highlight of the videogame. Lucia has recently been released from prison, while Jason is a former soldier who became involved with drug runners in the Leonida Keys. When a criminal job goes wrong, the pair become entangled in a wider conspiracy.

Based on the latest reports, the videogame is not on the cards for the official release in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

As per the official site, over 4,700 employees cutting across a dozen studios of Rockstar studios, devoted more than eight years to build the latest instalment of GTA. The active production only began after the release of Rockstar’s previous game, Red Dead Redemption II, in 2018. Earlier slated for a late 2025 release , the game’s launch was postponed twice owing to a series of leaks in 2022 and the online release of stolen gameplay videos.

Developers immersed themselves in the region while building the game, driving through Miami, the Florida Keys and surrounding communities, flying over the Everglades and researching the area’s history and architecture.

In a bid to cater to the immersive gameplay experience, the videogame allows players to tune into more than 20 radio stations at home or in their vehicles, with music ranging from Simple Minds and Daft Punk to Van Halen. A fresh addition in the latest instalment is podcasts. Among the options is a true-crime-style series chronicling Vice City, the game’s main metropolis.

The videogame’s plot unfolds by building the relationship between Jason and Lucia, from a chance encounter during a police stop to a robbery gone wrong that lands Lucia in jail. Much of the adventure transpires through lengthy cinematic cut-scenes, allowing players to sit back and watch the story. Only later does the game open up and hand players control of Jason’s day-to-day life, a former soldier working for local gangsters, who is recovering drug packages dropped at sea, stealing cars and shaking down debtors.

The videogame’s release has sparked a wave of excitement among gamers for detailed attention to the graphics. In GTA VI, the hair sways in the wind, muscles flex beneath clothing and characters move with a naturalism. The fictional state of Leonida, Rockstar’s take on Florida, enables a larger-than-life experience to the gamers. This is enveloped by bustling city streets, neon-soaked nightlife and pristine beaches all feature in a vast 3D world that players can explore while scuba diving.

Further, the game’s map is learnt to be one of the biggest and busiest ever made in the GTA-series history. The latest addition allows the non-player characters go about their own lives, and the world seems to carry on whether the player is involved or not. A simple drive across town might involve a random police traffic stop, witnessing a car accident or stumbling across a robbery by the beach.

Additionally, players are likely to find cars heavier in the latest instalment of the video-game, relatably tough to manoeuvre with a responsibility to keep an eye on their fuel tanks. They also decide what stays in a car trunk and what comes along for the ride, juggle phone calls and messages, and use apps to identify targets or track potential scores.

articles.title: IIIT-H students develop web plugin to translate text into Indian Sign Language
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The tool is a simple plugin that lets you select text on a web page, producing a 3D avatar that signs in the Indian Sign Language

The Indian Sign Language (ISL) uses gestures to represent complex words and sentences and has its own grammar and word order. People with hearing impairments find it a challenge to read content online. To address this gap, Masthan Sharif Shaik and Mohammed Raza, third-year BTech. students from the Center for Visual Information Technology (CVIT), IIIT-Hyderabad, under the supervision of Prof. C.V. Jawahar and Prof. Vinay Namboodiri (University of Bath, U.K.), developed a cost-effective plugin that can be added to any website.

The plugin can run inside a browser in real time, without any real hardware or an AI model running on a server. “Websites today support captions, screen readers, and high-contrast modes, but almost none of them can show content in sign language. Existing signing avatars are either costly motion-capture systems, heavy AI models that need powerful GPUs, or systems built from sign notation – all of which require linguistic experts and also tend to move robotically,” Sharif said.

The researchers first took the official Indian Sign Language Research And Training Centre’s sign-language dictionary videos and used computer vision to recover each signer’s 3D body, hand and finger movements. “Automatic reconstruction, however, often gets fingers wrong, and in sign language a wrong finger can change the meaning. So, we built an annotation tool, Gizmo, to correct only the few key poses of each sign instead of every frame,” Sharif said.

There is an offline preprocessing that takes place where sentences are converted into ISL word order. For example, a sentence such as “He will come home” in ISL becomes “He home come”. When a sentence like the former is highlighted and the ‘Click To Sign’ button is selected, the stored motion for each sign is fetched, and the signs are blended smoothly, allowing the avatar to sign the whole sentence fluidly. Words without a sign are fingerspelled letter by letter.

The movements are more natural in this case because the avatar replays motion captured from real signers rather than motion generated from notation. Additionally, what makes this task unique is that it all happens without a GPU. “The heavy computer-vision work happens once, offline, when the sign dictionary is built. Viewing a sentence only replays and blends stored motion together, which an ordinary laptop handles”, says Sharif.

When tested on deaf and hard-of-hearing signers, the ISL signers understood about 89% of sentences signed by the avatar. However, the lack of facial features in the avatar was cited as a drawback because expressions typically include grammar in ISL, as well as signs that change form in context. “We will work to incorporate this in our next iteration,” says Sharif.

“Indian Sign language (ISL) seriously lacks resources and technologies”, explains Prof. Jawahar. The group is working in two directions – Sign Language Synthesis as well as Sign Language Understanding. The plugin is related to sign language synthesis from text on low cost commodity hardware.

articles.title: India missed its 2025 TB elimination target. What does the WHO report show?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 has withheld India’s 2025 incidence estimate pending an assessment of new surveillance data. What does the report reveal about India’s TB burden, and why has the country missed its target?

The story so far: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the world’s tuberculosis (TB) burden despite expanded diagnosis and treatment services, falling short of the national target of eliminating TB by 2025. According to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report, released on November 12, 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025.

While India’s estimated TB mortality rate fell by 38%, from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 per lakh in 2025, the country diagnosed and notified 25.3 lakh cases during the year. However, the WHO has not published India’s estimated incidence for that year, as the figures are under review.

articles.title: OPEC share in India’s crude imports drops to 27.4% in Apr-Oct amid West Asia flare-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: During the mentioned period, India’s crude oil imports spurred about 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT)

The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries’ (OPEC) share in India’s crude oil basket declined sharply to 27.4% during April-October of the current fiscal, against 38.5% in the corresponding period last year, according to the latest provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC).

The decline potentially reflects a shift in India’s crude procurement strategy as the country navigates shipping disruptions and geopolitical uncertainties arising from the continuing conflict in West Asia.
During the seven-month period, India’s crude oil imports increased 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT).
Without identifying individual countries, PPAC data showed that supplies from the Eurasian region accounted for 43.8% of India’s crude oil import basket, while the Middle East contributed 36%.
South America accounted for 10.6% of imports, followed by Africa at 6.6% and North America at 3%.
The changing sourcing pattern indicates a growing diversification of India’s crude oil procurement, with supplies from outside the traditional Middle Eastern market gaining a larger share.

On the petroleum products trade front, diesel accounted for the largest share of India’s exports at 43.4% during the reported period. Petrol and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) followed with shares of 22.4% and 10%, respectively.
On the import side, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) constituted the largest component, accounting for 50.5% of total petroleum product imports, followed by petroleum coke (petcoke) at 18.3%.
Petroleum product exports remain an important component of India’s external energy trade to contain the impact on its net oil and gas import bill.
Further, PPAC data released on Wednesday showed that petroleum product export volumes declined 13.5% year-on-year during April-October, even as their export value increased approximately 47%.

articles.title: Israel army says it completed ground operation in central Gaza
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area
Israel's military said that a ground operation involving tanks in central Gaza that began the previous day despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire had come to an end on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The Defence Ministry's body in charge of civilian affairs in Palestinian territories, Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT), said in a statement that Palestinians would again be free to move in the targeted areas near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps.

"We would like to inform you that the activity has ended, and the Salah al-Din axis has been reopened," COGAT said in an Arabic-language statement on Facebook, referring to the war-shattered territory's main thoroughfare.

On Wednesday (November 18, 2026), the Israeli military said it had launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, beyond the so-called "Yellow Line" which separates areas under Israeli military and Hamas control following an October 2025 ceasefire.
An AFP journalist reported seeing Israeli tanks positioning themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp.
Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area.
The military said in a statement that the operation had been launched to "dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

A Gaza security source told AFP there had been "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".
Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal that came after two years of devastating war sparked by Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza Health Ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

articles.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on November 16

Climate negotiators stripped out any reference to ‌ending the use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft deal text published ​on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as the COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkiye, approaches its Friday (November 20, 2026) deadline.

The talks are ⁠taking place at a time when war and rising living costs are competing for the attention of policymakers and the public against the warming climate and its increasingly severe effects, including heatwaves, floods and droughts.

The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Monday's (November 16, 2026) two references to fossil fuels and limiting their use — a topic that ‌deeply ⁠divides nations in the negotiations every year — were removed, as was mention of a $120 ⁠billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.
"This new text has gone backwards from the one released earlier in the week," said Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank Power Shift Africa.
"If this version of ​the text remains, it will be a ‌ghost COP. The summit will have nothing to show for what happened here."

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft did retain an acknowledgement that global warming could exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold countries have sought to preserve, and the need for "deep, rapid and sustained" cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.
It also encouraged efforts ‌to scale up the deployment of technologies that can suck carbon out of the atmosphere, something ​scientists say would be needed to bring temperatures back down.

Australia, which is leading negotiations under a split presidency arrangement with Turkiye, previously ⁠said Monday's (November 16, 2026) opening draft of the deal was always intended to be a broad document that would then be narrowed down.

While the conference is scheduled to end on Friday (November 20, 2026), in recent years, efforts to secure ‌consensus among the nearly 200 countries participating have regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours.

📰 COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on November 16

Climate negotiators stripped out any reference to ‌ending the use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft deal text published ​on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as the COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkiye, approaches its Friday (November 20, 2026) deadline.

The talks are ⁠taking place at a time when war and rising living costs are competing for the attention of policymakers and the public against the warming climate and its increasingly severe effects, including heatwaves, floods and droughts.

The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Monday's (November 16, 2026) two references to fossil fuels and limiting their use — a topic that ‌deeply ⁠divides nations in the negotiations every year — were removed, as was mention of a $120 ⁠billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.

"This new text has gone backwards from the one released earlier in the week," said Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank Power Shift Africa.

"If this version of ​the text remains, it will be a ‌ghost COP. The summit will have nothing to show for what happened here."

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft did retain an acknowledgement that global warming could exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold countries have sought to preserve, and the need for "deep, rapid and sustained" cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.

It also encouraged efforts ‌to scale up the deployment of technologies that can suck carbon out of the atmosphere, something ​scientists say would be needed to bring temperatures back down.

Australia, which is leading negotiations under a split presidency arrangement with Turkiye, previously ⁠said Monday's (November 16, 2026) opening draft of the deal was always intended to be a broad document that would then be narrowed down.

While the conference is scheduled to end on Friday (November 20, 2026), in recent years, efforts to secure ‌consensus among the nearly 200 countries participating have regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours.

articles.title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort

A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday (November 19, 2026), after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.
Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti .

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.

The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort and fear being sidelined by Mr. Trump's direct talks with Mr. Putin.
“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Mr. Putin told reporters in Shenzhen, China.
He insisted the bridge is a civilian asset, adding that he had ordered the bridge closed to the transport of military hardware or ammunition.
Mr. Putin also said that the road side of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” but vowed to rebuild it.
The rail section is believed to be stronger than the road side, to bear the greater weight of cargo wagons.

The 19-kilometre (12-mile) Kerch Bridge is a key route for military and civilian supplies to Crimea, which Moscow seized in defiance of international law in 2014 and uses to support front-line troops. It is a potent reminder of Russia's illegal annexation of the territory and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, according to Mr. Zelenskyy, and the train track was damaged by domestically produced Neptune missiles, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said.

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi says Russia, Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks and agreed to keep communicating in the first such encounter between the two countries' leaders in seven years.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, she said she raised the issue of Moscow's treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia and urged Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for alleged spying during their meeting late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in Shenzhen, China.
“We reached an agreement to maintain communication at various levels, including direct contact between the president and myself,” Ms. Takaichi said.
Japan's ties with Russia have long been strained by a territorial dispute dating back decades.

Japan lodged a protest with Russia in October over the arrest of a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on suspicion of spying, demanding that Moscow provide an explanation, consular access and humane treatment.

Moscow recently seized control of some local subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco, the largest cigarette maker in Russia, and the company reported it expects a 724 billion yen ($4.5 billion) loss for this year due to the takeover.

Earlier, Japan Tobacco had forecast a 662 billion yen profit for the financial year ending December 31. The company said it has not given up legal ownership of the Russia-based subsidiaries or withdrawn from operating in Russia.

Tensions rose in August after Mr. Putin visited Iturup, one of four Russian-controlled islands off Japan's northern coast that Tokyo also claims. Earlier this month, Tokyo protested after two Russian aircraft briefly violated Japanese airspace off southwestern Japan.

The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Mr. Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Mr. Putin is attending the annual APEC summit for the first time in nine years. He, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a summit meeting on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after the APEC gathering, an event that seems to underscore Japan's diminished role as a global power.

articles.title: Rohingya a ‘distinct lineage’ close to Bangladeshis and Burmese: Study
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The International Court of Justice held that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in the north Rakhine State

The Rohingya are a distinct genetic group with genomic ancestry closer to Bangladeshis but considerable genetic mixture from the Burmese lineage. While this isn’t surprising from a linguistic-cultural perspective, it is the first such comprehensive study from a genomic analysis perspective.

“Burmese” here is a stand-in for East and Southeast Asian ancestry in general. The study underlines what is now a basic principle of human population genetics that all ethnic populations are a result of intermingling of multiple population groups through history.

The analysis comes on the heels of a Thursday (November 19) verdict by the International Court of Justice. In a 9-6 ruling, the court held that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in the north Rakhine State. This was the verdict on a 2019 case brought to the court by The Gambia in which it accused the Myanmar government of trying to destroy the Rohingya.
The Burmese state has tried to portray the Rohingya as “outsiders” from Bangladesh to justify atrocities against them.

The genetics study, which appeared on November 17 in the peer-reviewed journal Scientific Reports , does not say anything about citizenship, but notes: “This study addresses a critical void in the evolutionary history of a deeply marginalised group and unequivocally reinforces that modern human populations are intricate mosaics of diverse ancestral lineages, fundamentally shaped by historical migrations and gene flow that transcend contemporary political boundaries.”

The main authors of the study are affiliated with a range of institutions including the Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi; BRIC-Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD), Hyderabad; the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh; University of Calcutta; and Amity University, Uttar Pradesh.

“Our analyses reveal a complex genomic architecture that closely mirrors their linguistic affiliations. The Rohingya exhibit a foundational genetic affinity with eastern South Asian Indo-European speaking populations, predominantly aligning with present-day Bangladeshi communities,” the authors report.

The Rohingya migrated into the Arakan region within the last millennium and, following this, the ancestral Rohingya mixed with those with Southeast Asian ancestry from local Myanmar-related populations, they underline.

For their analysis, the researchers took blood samples from 25 Rohingya volunteers at the Cox’s Bazar refugee camp in Bangladesh, with informed consent and ethics approval from the University of Dhaka. For comparison they sampled 45 neighbours: 27 Bangladeshi Muslims, nine Bangladeshi Hindus, and nine people from the Bawm tribal community. They then merged these results with published data from around the world, for a final dataset of 2,217 people. Each person’s DNA was read at about 370,000 key places along the genome, where nucleotide letters commonly differ between people.

articles.title: Why data interoperability is critical to the future of hospital care
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The future of critical care will be defined by how effectively the information is connected, interpreted and applied

In an intensive care unit, every second matters. A critically ill patient may be connected to several devices, including patient monitors, ventilators and infusion pumps, while laboratory systems and electronic health records continuously generate additional information. Together, these systems create a large and rapidly-changing picture of the patient’s condition. However, when the information remains fragmented across devices and platforms, clinicians may spend valuable time locating, verifying and reconciling data before they can act.

This makes interoperability a clinical priority in critical care, not simply an information technology requirement. Integration enables systems to exchange data, but true interoperability ensures that the information being exchanged is accurate, interpretable and clinically relevant. This can help care teams coordinate and prioritise interventions more effectively while reducing the need to move between multiple systems to assemble a clinical picture.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Why data interoperability is critical to the future of hospital care. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

The future of critical care will be defined by how effectively the information is connected, interpreted and applied

In an intensive care unit, every second matters. A critically ill patient may be connected to several devices, including patient monitors, ventilators and infusion pumps, while laboratory systems and electronic health records continuously generate additional information. Together, these systems create a large and rapidly-changing picture of the patient’s condition. However, when the information remains fragmented across devices and platforms, clinicians may spend valuable time locating, verifying and reconciling data before they can act.

This makes interoperability a clinical priority in critical care, not simply an information technology requirement. Integration enables systems to exchange data, but true interoperability ensures that the information being exchanged is accurate, interpretable and clinically relevant. This can help care teams coordinate and prioritise interventions more effectively while reducing the need to move between multiple systems to assemble a clinical picture.

articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia

The story so far: The battle for the most sought after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer after the U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule (IFR) barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia. The new, yet to be published, rule also restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”
The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but a legal tool to control the flow took shape only during the first Trump term when the administration passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It gave the U.S. a legal weapon to control the movement of advanced technology originating from the country. Its primary purpose was to curb export of top-tier chips that had dual-use — both commercial and military purposes — to countries like China, Russia and Iran.
