articles.title: Hyderabad doctor brings down rare disease drug cost from ₹9 crore to ₹2.5 lakh; seven children to get free treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30; the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year

Imagine having a medicine that could help manage your child’s rare genetic condition, but being unable to afford it because a year’s treatment costs as much as ₹9 crore. For seven families in India, that situation could soon change.

Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30, following an initiative led by Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

The development is significant not just because the families will receive the medicine without paying for it, but also because its cost has been brought down through pharmaceutical compounding in the Netherlands. While the commercial version of the drug costs approximately ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child annually, the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year.

The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.

The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.

Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr. Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.

Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr. Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.

The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.

According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.

While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr. Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.

Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30; the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year

Imagine having a medicine that could help manage your child’s rare genetic condition, but being unable to afford it because a year’s treatment costs as much as ₹9 crore. For seven families in India, that situation could soon change.

Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30, following an initiative led by Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

The development is significant not just because the families will receive the medicine without paying for it, but also because its cost has been brought down through pharmaceutical compounding in the Netherlands. While the commercial version of the drug costs approximately ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child annually, the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year.

The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.

The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.

Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr. Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.

Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr. Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.

The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.

According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.

While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr. Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.

articles.title: GTA VI generates record $1.1 billion pre-order revenue
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year

As Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI officially launches today , November 19, 2026, a market intelligence report from Sensor Tower highlights an unprecedented shift in consumer engagement and industry revenue.

According to Sensor Tower’s report, the title generated $1.1 billion in pre-order revenue globally across PlayStation and Xbox consoles prior to release, with 11.3 million copies sold. This accomplishment marks the largest pre-launch revenue total on record.

The analytics firms project that total sales could reach $3.2 billion by the end of 2026. Beyond financial performance, the report forecasts a noticeable reallocation of consumer attention across the broader digital landscape.
Daily active user metrics across competing games and entertainment platforms are expected to see a measurable decline as players engage with the new release.
Sensor Tower estimates the average GTA VI player age at approximately 34 years old. This audience displays high companion engagement on second-screen platforms, including Discord, TikTok, and Twitch.
With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year.

On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.summary: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal
articles.keyPoints:
• Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal
• Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.
• Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Jharkhand SIR: Final BLO meetings at poll stations on November 18
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jharkhand CEO K Ravi Kumar appeals to all eligible Indian citizens in the state to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll by taking part in Ek Aur Avsar (One More Opportunity) camps

Jharkhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) K. Ravi Kumar on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) appealed to all eligible Indian citizens in the State to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll being published under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

Speaking to the media in Ranchi, Mr. Ravi asserted that an “Ek Aur Avsar” (One More Opportunity) camp will be held on November 18 at all polling stations in the State, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., where meetings of BLOs (Booth Level Officers) and BLAs-2 (Booth Level Agents-2) will take place in the form of a “Chunav Pathshala” (Electoral Awareness Session).

He pointed out that the objective of this special initiative is to provide one additional opportunity for any eligible Indian citizen who, for various reasons, has not yet had their name added to the electoral roll.

Mr. Ravi explained that the camps will focus primarily on three key areas. First, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is republishing the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) list at all polling stations. If any eligible Indian citizen has been included in this list, they may follow the prescribed procedure to submit Form-6 or an enumeration form.

Second, lists of voters in categories such as “No Mapping” or those with “Logical Discrepancies”—who have failed to provide the necessary documentation despite receiving two notices from the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and undergoing a door-to-door verification process—will be made available at the respective polling stations.

Third, efforts are being made to identify eligible Indian citizens who will have turned 18 by October 1, 2026, but who have not yet registered their names in the electoral roll for their respective polling stations. Eligible Indian citizens will be able to have their names included in the electoral roll by submitting Form 6.

The CEO said that this is the sixth and final BLO-BLA-2 meeting being held under the ongoing SIR process in Jharkhand. He urged all eligible citizens in the state to take advantage of this opportunity and get their names added to the electoral roll, ensuring that no eligible Indian citizen remains excluded.

The ECI has already extended the deadline for final publication of electoral rolls in Jharkhand under the SIR to November 30. The final publication was initially scheduled for October 7 and was later extended to October 19 before being revised.

articles.title: Construction activities on Kaziranga wildlife corridors flagged
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: An Eastern Assam-based environment activist writes to the Supreme Court-constituted Central Empowered Committee, highlighting the concerns

An eastern Assam-based environmental activist has reminded the Supreme Court–constituted Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to continue construction activities on the wildlife corridors of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve.

Kaziranga has nine notified wildlife corridors and several dandis or animal pathways. Animals use these corridors and dandis mostly to escape to the hills of Karbi Anglong district when the park is flooded during the monsoon months.

In a letter to the CEC’s Member-Secretary on November 16, Rohit Choudhury said he had brought such construction activities to the notice of the Committee on May 11. He lamented the lack of action against these activities, violating the Supreme Court’s April 2019 order.

“We order that all kinds of mining and related activities along the aforesaid Kaziranga National Park area and in the entire catchment area of rivers, streams and rivulets originating in the Karbi Anglong Hill ranges and flowing into Kaziranga National Park, including the Tiger Reserve, are restrained. No new construction shall be permitted on private lands which form part of the nine identified animal corridors,” the apex court’s order read.

“Despite this clear and categorical prohibition, the Government of Assam has displayed a disturbing disregard for the mandate of the Supreme Court by permitting and facilitating unlawful construction activities within these ecologically sensitive wildlife corridors,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

He reminded the CEC of photographic evidence of a building under construction on the Haldhibari Wildlife Corridor attached to his May 11 letter. “The construction activity was allowed to proceed unabated and has now reached an advanced stage of completion,” he wrote, attaching recent photographs of the construction site.

Mr. Choudhury said the CEC’s inability to take up the matter six months ago “effectively afforded the concerned authorities sufficient time to continue and substantially complete the illegal construction”.
He said such delays in addressing matters of grave environmental significance seriously undermine the purpose and efficacy of the CEC’s mandate.
The activist further said the CEC did not inform the Supreme Court of any violation of its April 12, 2019, order for necessary action.

“This persistent failure of enforcement has emboldened continued violations and weakened the protection envisaged by the Supreme Court,” he said, urging the CEC to recommend contempt proceedings against the officials responsible for permitting, facilitating or failing to prevent these blatant violations of the court’s binding directions.

articles.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 65.65 lakh pilgrims visit four Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026 as Badrinath portals close for winter

Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year.
According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard.
Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025.
The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added.

To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.”

The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation.

Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November.

Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. The foundation attributed the higher cumulative numbers partly to a longer pilgrimage season and fewer weather-related disruptions. Kedarnath remained operational for 204 days, compared with 175 days last year.

The SDC Foundation report also flagged concerns over pilgrim safety, recording 297 fatalities across the five shrines in 2026, compared with 182 in 2025. Health-related natural deaths alone increased by 81%, from 159 to 288, with Kedarnath accounting for 142 such deaths.

Vehicle movement during the Char Dham Yatra also witnessed a significant rise, increasing from 5,14,016 in 2025 to 6,68,877 in 2026 (till November 14). This represents an increase of 1,54,861 vehicles, or more than 30% over the previous year.

articles.title: Ruckus erupts between SFI activists and police over setting up bookstalls near Calcutta University
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The SFI leaders said they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a bookstall on the College Street footpath, but police refused on November 16 evening, saying it could disrupt traffic

A ruckus erupted between supporters of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and police near the University of Kolkata for setting up a book stall. After the clash, police detained several SFI supporters, including the SFI State secretary, Debanjan Dey.

The SFI leadership said that they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a book stall at a makeshift stall on the footpath of College Street. However, the police refused to grant permission on Monday evening, stating that it might disrupt traffic. The book stall was part of a three-day campaign, “Sangrami Boipotro”, by the party. It was supposed to be inaugurated by the Left Front chairman, Biman Bose, on Tuesday evening.

“We have permission from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Jorasanko Police Station for a period of five years to set up bookstalls at College Street. Necessary tax was also paid to the concerned authorities. We have been setting up such stalls for the last four years. Our plan was to do the same this year too. But the Kolkata Police have now refused to allow us anymore,” said Mr. Dey to the media persons

The protesters said that a few police vans had already been stationed on College Street since Monday night. When they began preparing to set up the stalls on Tuesday morning, the police stopped them and said that no book stalls could be organised in the area.

The situation escalated when they blocked College Street and staged a sit-in. They laid out a sheet on the tram line in the middle of the road and began selling their books. They also invited the police to buy books for their children. It immediately resulted in a clash with the police. The police were seen using mild force to disrupt the protesters and clear the road. Several activists, including Mr. Dey, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, Didhiti Roy, and Haseeb Hossain, have been detained.

“A heavy police force was deployed across College Street on Tuesday only to stop us selling some books. They have assaulted the students who have been fighting for the books. It is now clear that the government has declared war against the books. They want to destroy the culture and tradition of Bengal. We will have to fight the battle with books only against them,” said Mr. Dey after the detention.
Following the development, the left student union also organised a rally in the evening at the Mahabodhi Society and demanded the immediate release of the detained students.

The dispute over the book stalls set up by the Left parties began during Durga Puja. Police and civic bodies demolished several stalls set up by the parties across Kolkata. In Jadavpur, a bulldozer was also brought in to dismantle a stall, sparking a huge political controversy. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had described Left party supporters as “atheist” and declared that they would not be allowed to set up their book stalls near puja pandals, where such stalls have been a fixture for decades.

articles.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner

A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
It also follows recent security scares at two British air force bases hosting the U.S. military, with officials accusing Iran of involvement in plots to target them.
A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner.

Held in British police custody since his November 10 arrest near Gloucester, southwest England, he was handed to the US military “over suspected national security and espionage allegations”, U.K. Counter Terrorism Policing said.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the decision to “pass the investigation to them to progress” followed an extensive probe by his counter-terror unit and subsequent discussions between British prosecutors and “American partners”.
FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that the unnamed Army officer was in U.S. custody after “an espionage investigation”.
He noted it had involved “close cooperation” between the FBI’s Philadelphia field office and various other US and UK law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
“Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action,” Mr. Patel added.

A senior NATO military official last week confirmed that the arrested soldier had been assigned to its Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), the alliance’s 20-nation, high-readiness force led by the British Army.

articles.title: Why frontline experience and operational research need to come together in the health sector
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The field worker knows which question matters; the researcher brings the systematic approach and methodological rigour needed to investigate it

articles.title: Earthshot Prize: Climate action needs innovation, global cooperation, say leaders on green carpet in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations

Global leaders, business executives, and celebrities called for greater investment in environmental innovations and collective action against climate change as they gathered on the green carpet ahead of the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
Among those attending were former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern, Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla, filmmaker Karan Johar, and Maharashtra Environment Minister Pankaja Mund.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Poonawalla emphasised the importance of supporting environmental innovations and helping them attract investment.

“Prevention is better than cure—that’s what we believe at Serum Institute,” he said, explaining the company’s partnership with the Earthshot Prize. He added that the initiative would help innovators connect with investors and scale up technologies capable of addressing environmental challenges.
Ms. Ardern welcomed the awards to Mumbai, highlighting India’s record of producing the highest number of Earthshot finalists and winners.

“The Earthshot Prize is showcasing responses to that crisis to demonstrate that things are happening and innovation is available, we just need to scale it up with speed,” she said, referring to the climate crisis.

Coral Pasisi, president of Tofia, Niue, highlighted Indigenous-led ocean conservation efforts. “We’re protecting one of the largest areas of ocean on the planet. And we developed a sustainable financing mechanism that’s driven by Indigenous people,” she said, stressing the need for international support.

Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations. She expressed concern that rapid urbanisation and industrialisation had drowned out natural sounds, including birdsong and flowing water, and urged people to protect forests and biodiversity.
Filmmaker Karan Johar praised Prince William’s environmental commitment, describing him as a “climate warrior” who empowered innovators through the Earthshot Prize.

Actor Sonam Kapoor emphasised that environmental responsibility extended beyond public statements. Speaking about her children, she said individuals and governments needed to take concrete steps to protect the environment for future generations.

articles.title: Fearmongering around fake drugs
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As per the last National Drug Survey published in 2017, the volume of counterfeit drugs in the Indian market detected in the survey was at a negligible 0.0245%

Recent news from Karnataka regarding the seizure of fake cancer drugs from a licensed distributor during a raid has understandably sparked concerns. Counterfeit drugs for serious conditions like cancer are a sensational and emotive issue, often provoking a demand for severe action, including death sentences for those involved in the distribution.

However, in this case, there is a serious reason to doubt the authenticity of the news reports about the recent seizure since the Government of Karnataka has not confirmed that indeed counterfeit cancer drugs were seized in the raid. While a purported list of the drugs seized was circulated on social media, it only contained antibiotics, not cancer drugs. The silence of the State Health Department on the news reports about the counterfeit drugs is insensitive to the dread and uncertainty being faced by patients receiving cancer treatment, not to mention the doubts of those wondering whether they lost their loved ones to cancer because of counterfeit drugs. The Department should clear the air on the matter by issuing a press release or holding a press conference. If counterfeit cancer drugs were indeed seized, the government should release the names of the drugs and the hospitals possibly affected. If not, it should at least communicate the same to the public. Letting the uncertainty hang without authoritative answers is not in public interest.
Science, Space & Environment Report: Fearmongering around fake drugs. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Transgender rights, healthcare should not be compromised
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Clinical understanding of the care needs of a transgender person remains rudimentary in India. Doctors, nurses, receptionists, security staff and hospital administrators need to be trained in basic transgender health.

Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 earlier this year. The new Act represents a significant shift from the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The 2026 amendment removes the principle of self-identification and demands a medical board’s recommendation; a selection from prescribed categories; and certification by a District Magistrate. It fundamentally changes legal recognition for transgender persons from self-identification to medical assessment. While the 2026 Act does increase protection, it changes the philosophical foundation of transgender rights — from recognition based substantially on autonomy and self-identification towards recognition mediated by medical and administrative authorities.

The definition of “transgender” as introduced in the Amendment Act is in contradiction to established international evidence and guidelines laid down in the World Health Organization ICD-11 and the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care Version 8.

articles.title: Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility among the five winners of Earthshot Prize

Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
He was speaking at the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony, which was held in India for the first time.

“India is a nation of extraordinary innovation, ambition, facing immense environmental pressures, yet moving ahead with determination. Not because the challenge is simple, not because the path is easy. But because millions of people have decided that progress simply cannot wait,” said Prince William.
Winners of the Earthshot Prize award were declared under five categories in a glittering ceremony. The awardees include the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility.
“They [Gen Z] are bringing fresh ideas and showing what is possible when optimism is matched with action. Their ideas, their energy, and their determination are helping to shape the future,” he said.
During his address, Prince William reflected on the achievements of this year’s finalists and the growing global movement behind environmental innovation.
The ceremony was attended by environmental innovators, philanthropists, business leaders, government representatives and global figures from sport, entertainment and culture.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Earthshot Prize in the ‘Clean Our Air’ category. Accepting the award, the company’s CEO, Suman Mishra, said it showed how urgent optimism worked.
The company has won 1 million pounds for its efforts, due to which 33 per cent of India’s three-wheelers are now electric.

Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

“They [Gen Z] are bringing fresh ideas and showing what is possible when optimism is matched with action. Their ideas, their energy, and their determination are helping to shape the future,” he said.

The ceremony was attended by environmental innovators, philanthropists, business leaders, government representatives and global figures from sport, entertainment and culture.

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Earthshot Prize in the ‘Clean Our Air’ category. Accepting the award, the company’s CEO, Suman Mishra, said it showed how urgent optimism worked.

The company has won 1 million pounds for its efforts, due to which 33 per cent of India’s three-wheelers are now electric.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Over 50 students of Keralam school hospitalised after suspected pollution from tar-mixing unit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Panchayat authorities had earlier issued a stop memo against the tar-mixing plant located close to the school in Kollam. However, it resumed operations after obtaining court permission, local residents claimed

Several students of a private school at Kottiyam in Kollam district of Keralam were hospitalised on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) with breathing difficulties, itching and other complaints allegedly linked to pollution from a nearby tar-mixing unit, the police said.
Around 55 to 60 students from different classes were affected, according to local representatives and residents.
The students complained of physical discomfort and breathing difficulties, prompting the school authorities to arrange emergency medical assistance.
Around eight ambulances were deployed to transport the affected students to a nearby hospital for treatment, local authorities said.
The incident has raised concerns over the operation of a tar-mixing plant located close to the school.
The panchayat authorities had earlier issued a stop memo against the plant. However, it resumed operations after obtaining court permission, local residents claimed.
Health complaints among students emerged after the plant resumed operations, they added.
The police and panchayat authorities have intervened following the incident.

articles.title: Annamalai flays TVK-led govt. over delay in appointing Cauvery technical cell vice-chairman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The delay in filling such a crucial position raises questions about the government’s administrative efficiency and sense of responsibility, he says

We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) termed as unacceptable the delay in appointing the vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing by the Tamil Nadu government.

In a post on X, Mr. Annamalai said the resignation of M. Selvaraj, who served as vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing, was accepted on June 28, 2026. However, the Government Order (G.O.) to fill this post was issued only on October 9, 2026. Even more than a month after the issuance of the G.O., there is no information so far on the appointment of a new vice-chairman.

The delay in filling such a crucial position, which plays a significant role in safeguarding Tamil Nadu’s water rights and dealing with inter-State river water disputes, raises questions about the government’s administrative efficiency and sense of responsibility. This is not an ordinary administrative post but one that involves important technical and legal responsibilities in protecting Tamil Nadu’s water rights, he said.

On the one hand, farmers in the Cauvery delta districts are worried over the lack of adequate water for Samba cultivation. On the other, the Cauvery water-sharing dispute continues, while Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu dam project remains a challenge to Tamil Nadu’s rights. “At a time when the State is confronted with several such critical issues, the vacancy in the key post of vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing is nothing but a serious administrative failure,” he said.

Reports have emerged that Tamil Nadu Ministers N. Anand and Aadhav Arjuna are set to meet the Union Minister for Jal Shakti and submit a representation on the Mekedatu dam issue. “Does the TVK government believe that meeting a Union Minister and submitting a representation alone will resolve these issues, without strengthening the State’s own administrative machinery and making timely appointments to key positions?” Mr. Annamalai questioned.

Such administrative delays and lack of accountability by the TVK government in matters of such significance, which concern the livelihoods of farmers and Tamil Nadu’s water rights, are wholly unacceptable, he added.

articles.title: DC inspects public parks in Yadgir, orders anti-encroachment drive and formation of ward committees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid widespread complaints that open public spaces were being encroached upon due to the lack of boundary walls, Mr. Pandve stressed the need for immediate protective measures.

​To curb the encroachment of government land, rejuvenate public parks, and expedite the resolution of civic issues, Yadgir Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve has directed the City Municipal Council (CMC) Commissioner to constitute citizen committees across every ward in the city.

​Accompanied by Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar and CMC Commissioner Umesh Chavan, the Deputy Commissioner conducted a spot inspection of several public parks in Gandhi Nagar and Wards 25 and 26 on Monday (November 16) morning to assess their present condition.

​Taking serious note of widespread complaints that open public spaces were being encroached upon due to the lack of boundary walls around hundreds of parks in the city, Mr. Pandve stressed the need for immediate protective measures.

As a priority, he instructed the CMC Commissioner to immediately construct a compound wall, undertake sapling plantation, and install a signage board at the park located on the stretch leading to Gandhi Nagar.

​Emphasising participatory governance to enhance the city’s aesthetics and address local civic grievances effectively, the Deputy Commissioner directed officials to form dedicated ward-level committees without delay. He specified that these panels must be inclusive, comprising senior citizens, advocates, youth, women, and intellectuals, and must begin functioning immediately.

​During the inspection, local residents interacted with the Deputy Commissioner, the Superintendent of Police, and the CMC Commissioner to highlight pressing civic issues in their respective neighbourhoods.
​CMC Engineer Rakesh Reddy, Environmental Engineer Prashanth, and staff member Sharanamma were present during the visit.

articles.title: Andhra’s first semiconductor plant to come up near Visakhapatnam with ₹2,387 crore investment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The chip assembly and testing unit at Tarluvada is the State’s first project under the India Semiconductor Mission and will create 1,000 jobs

Andhra Pradesh is set to mark its entry into the high-technology semiconductor manufacturing sector with Advanced System In Package Technologies Private Limited establishing an Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility at Tarluvada village in Anandapuram mandal of Visakhapatnam district.

Cleared with a total proposed investment of ₹2,387.81 crore across two phases, the facility is projected to generate direct employment for 1,000 people, beginning with an outlay of ₹542.19 crore and 200 jobs in Phase I, followed by ₹1,845.61 crore and 800 jobs in Phase II.

In the global microelectronics value chain, an OSAT unit performs the crucial back-end stages of chip production. It takes fabricated silicon wafers and carries out precision assembly, protective encapsulation and rigorous electrical testing before the finished integrated circuits are deployed in mobile devices, telecommunications gear, consumer electronics and automotive systems.

Approved by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) on August 20, 2025, the Tarluvada plant holds strategic significance as the first ISM-sanctioned project to be grounded in Andhra Pradesh.

By building domestic capacity in chip packaging and testing, the project addresses a critical link in India’s semiconductor supply chain while anchoring a high-value electronics ecosystem on the east coast.

To expedite the project, the State government has rolled out an extensive package of fiscal, land and infrastructure support under the Andhra Pradesh Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy (4.0), 2024–29. Following clearance by the State Council of Ministers on February 24, 2026, the Information Technology, Electronics and Communications (IT, E&C) Department issued formal orders on February 27, 2026, treating the venture as a “special case” in view of its status as the State’s maiden ISM project.

Under the order, the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) will allot 30 acres of land at Tarluvada at a nominal rate of ₹1 per acre. The State will also extend special incentives of up to 40% of the project cost on a pari passu basis alongside the Government of India’s 50% grant disbursement.

The chip assembly and testing unit at Tarluvada is the State’s first project under the India Semiconductor Mission and will create 1,000 jobs

Andhra Pradesh is set to mark its entry into the high-technology semiconductor manufacturing sector with Advanced System In Package Technologies Private Limited establishing an Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility at Tarluvada village in Anandapuram mandal of Visakhapatnam district.

Cleared with a total proposed investment of ₹2,387.81 crore across two phases, the facility is projected to generate direct employment for 1,000 people, beginning with an outlay of ₹542.19 crore and 200 jobs in Phase I, followed by ₹1,845.61 crore and 800 jobs in Phase II.

In the global microelectronics value chain, an OSAT unit performs the crucial back-end stages of chip production. It takes fabricated silicon wafers and carries out precision assembly, protective encapsulation and rigorous electrical testing before the finished integrated circuits are deployed in mobile devices, telecommunications gear, consumer electronics and automotive systems.

Approved by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) on August 20, 2025, the Tarluvada plant holds strategic significance as the first ISM-sanctioned project to be grounded in Andhra Pradesh.

By building domestic capacity in chip packaging and testing, the project addresses a critical link in India’s semiconductor supply chain while anchoring a high-value electronics ecosystem on the east coast.

To expedite the project, the State government has rolled out an extensive package of fiscal, land and infrastructure support under the Andhra Pradesh Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy (4.0), 2024–29. Following clearance by the State Council of Ministers on February 24, 2026, the Information Technology, Electronics and Communications (IT, E&C) Department issued formal orders on February 27, 2026, treating the venture as a “special case” in view of its status as the State’s maiden ISM project.

The State will also extend special incentives of up to 40% of the project cost on a pari passu basis alongside the Government of India’s 50% grant disbursement.

“Work has started on the ground. All statutory clearances have been issued proactively by the State government, and the Government of India has also approved all clearances on its end. articles.title: KUDA allocates ₹1.91 crore for drinking water supply in Kalaburagi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under the allocation, 65% of the funds (₹1.24 crore) will be released to the Kalaburagi City Corporation, while the remaining 35% (₹67 lakh), will go to the Rural Drinking Water and Sanitation Department.

In an initiative to address the drinking water crisis, the Kalaburagi Urban Development Authority (KUDA) has approved an allocation of ₹1.91 crore from water cess funds to strengthen drinking water infrastructure in Kalaburagi city and its surrounding areas. articles.title: Apologised to prevent divisions among Hindus: Bageshwar Dham’s Dhirendra Shastri
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Explaining his position, he said that while demons and evil forces disrupted religious rituals in ancient times, those opposing such activities today attempted to create obstacles through social media posts

Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Krishna Shastri on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) said Sanatan Dharma faced a greater threat from "tainted elements" within Hindu society than from external forces, asserting that he had apologised for his recent controversial remarks to prevent divisions among Hindus and maintain social unity.

Mr. Shastri was recently embroiled in a controversy over remarks comparing Lord Ram and Lord Krishna during a religious discourse in Madhya Pradesh. He subsequently apologised, saying he had no intention of insulting either deity.

The controversy prompted Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav to demand cancellation of his programmes and a ban on permitting him to hold religious events in Uttar Pradesh, accusing him of hurting religious sentiments and disturbing social harmony ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

Speaking to local reporters on Tuesday (November 17) evening after delivering a discourse at a Ram Katha programme in Kunda's Beti area of Pratapgarh, Shastri said his apology was intended to ensure that Hindus did not fight among themselves.

Explaining his position, he said that while demons and evil forces disrupted religious rituals in ancient times, those opposing such activities today attempted to create obstacles through social media posts.
Mr. Shastri said the real meaning of Ram Rajya was ensuring justice, respect and equal opportunities for every individual in society.
He urged devotees to follow the ideals of Lord Ram in their daily lives and remain committed to religious values and traditions.
He asserted that his "campaign to strengthen Sanatan Dharma and Hindu society" would continue as long as he was alive, regardless of threats, opposition or pressure.
"Even if you shoot me, the campaign to propagate Sanatan Dharma will not stop," he said.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Explaining his position, he said that while demons and evil forces disrupted religious rituals in ancient times, those opposing such activities today attempted to create obstacles through social media posts

Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Krishna Shastri on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) said Sanatan Dharma faced a greater threat from "tainted elements" within Hindu society than from external forces, asserting that he had apologised for his recent controversial remarks to prevent divisions among Hindus and maintain social unity.

Mr. Shastri was recently embroiled in a controversy over remarks comparing Lord Ram and Lord Krishna during a religious discourse in Madhya Pradesh. He subsequently apologised, saying he had no intention of insulting either deity.

The controversy prompted Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav to demand cancellation of his programmes and a ban on permitting him to hold religious events in Uttar Pradesh, accusing him of hurting religious sentiments and disturbing social harmony ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

Speaking to local reporters on Tuesday (November 17) evening after delivering a discourse at a Ram Katha programme in Kunda's Beti area of Pratapgarh, Shastri said his apology was intended to ensure that Hindus did not fight among themselves.

Explaining his position, he said that while demons and evil forces disrupted religious rituals in ancient times, those opposing such activities today attempted to create obstacles through social media posts.

Mr. Shastri said the real meaning of Ram Rajya was ensuring justice, respect and equal opportunities for every individual in society.

He urged devotees to follow the ideals of Lord Ram in their daily lives and remain committed to religious values and traditions.

He asserted that his "campaign to strengthen Sanatan Dharma and Hindu society" would continue as long as he was alive, regardless of threats, opposition or pressure.

"Even if you shoot me, the campaign to propagate Sanatan Dharma will not stop," he said.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank chair backs CEO after reports expose past lapses; Trump calls tax leak ‘illegal’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Reports cite 15 million leaked records reviewed by more than 200 journalists; German Finance Minister calls for authorities to investigate

Deutsche Bank’s chairman backed ​his CEO Christian Sewing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) after a huge cache of leaked internal records renewed scrutiny ⁠of the German lender’s past dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, U.S. President Donald Trump and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The reports, compiled by a consortium of international journalists and published by outlets including Der Spiegel , the Financial Times , the New York Times and Le ‌Monde , examined Deutsche Bank’s dealings with Mr. Trump, Epstein and Russian oligarchs, including its pursuit of business in Russia before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Deutsche Bank, whose shares fell by as much as 6%, ‌said the matters in the various reports “date back many years”, and that the bank had since strengthened its ‌controls.
Christian Sewing, Chief Executive Officer of Deutsche Bank | Photo Credit: Reuters

“During ⁠my tenure, I haven’t seen a single decision from Christian Sewing that I was not comfortable ⁠with,” Deutsche Bank Chairman Alexander Wynaendts said in an emailed statement. Mr. Sewing has led Germany’s biggest lender since 2018.

The Financial Times reported that Deutsche Bank had inadvertently sent a Trump tax document to another client’s accountant in 2017 when the President was a Deutsche Bank client during his first ​term in office.
Asked in Manila about the ‌error, Mr. Trump said the bank should not have disclosed it. “They shouldn’t have done it. It’s illegal for them to do it,” Mr. Trump said.
Deutsche Bank declined to comment on Mr. Trump’s reaction.

The leaks also showed that Deutsche Bank was ambitious in pursuing business in Russia, including with high-profile oligarchs, right up to the invasion ‌of Ukraine in February 2022, even as some of the bank’s managers voiced concerns over the risks, according ​to the publications.

German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil called on authorities to investigate “and take the necessary action”. Deutsche Bank, he said, needs to explain “with complete transparency” how it has fixed failures and will ⁠prevent new ones.

articles.title: Iran army says it targeted U.S. military base in Kuwait
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster

The Iranian army claimed early on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) it targeted U.S. Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait with drones, triggering the air defence alerts in the oil-rich Gulf country for the first time in weeks.
The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster.
U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. forces in the West Asia, did not immediately comment.

Earlier on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Kuwait’s Army said its air defences were intercepting drone attacks but did not immediately report any damage. The country’s Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated Iranian “criminal” attacks and said they threatened Kuwait’s security and stability.

Iran also recently claimed attacks against U.S. military targets in the tiny island kingdom of Bahrain. Iran targeted U.S. facilities and interests in the neighbouring Gulf countries following the U.S. and Israeli strikes against it on Feb 28.

articles.title: Why did the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: What triggered the resurgence of measles in the U.S.? Is vaccine hesitancy putting decades of progress against measles at risk? How is the global measles surge affecting India?

The story so far: After 26 years of holding on to its measles elimination status, the United States lost this distinction. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO) revoked the United States’ measles elimination status. This was after over 5400 cases of measles were reported in the U.S. in 2026.

This is the highest annual total since 1989-91, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention(CDC). As per data put out by the Unicef, 96% of cases are in unvaccinated people or those with unknown vaccination status. Children under five account for 18% of cases and those aged 5-19 for 40%.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Why did the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? | Explained. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu
The Israeli Parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday (November 18, 2026), a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu. Eisenkot's bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu's most contentious policies following Kahana's election.

He was approved as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, backed by the Jewish-led opposition parties and by the Arab-led parties. The candidate backed by Netanyahu's bloc, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.
"The appointment of Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker is a worthy democratic move that reflects the absolute majority in favour of change," Mr. Eisenkot said ahead of the vote.

The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority. Mr. Eisenkot was subsequently given the task by Israel's president to try to form a new coalition government.

Mr. Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure enough alliances to form a coalition. As negotiations continue on the sidelines, his bloc, along with unaffiliated Arab-led parties, can use their majority in the newly-sworn in Knesset to advance their legislative agenda. They introduced several bills last week, including to set term limits on the role of prime minister, to form a government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023, attacks and to reverse laws to limit the powers of the judiciary.
Mr. Kahana gives the opposition bloc a major legislative advantage, according to Assaf Shapira with the Israel Democracy Institute, a Jerusalem think tank.
"It's important because there is not much time, because the speaker of the Knesset can make the legislative process much, much faster or much slower," Shapira said.
Mr. Kahana replaced Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, as speaker.

Mr. Eisenkot and his allies are under pressure to swiftly advance their legislative priorities in the weeks ahead. Currently a member of Eisenkot's Yashar party, Roy Folkman, heads the temporary committee that decides much of the Knesset's work until a government is formed.

fullParagraphs: The two-day visit comes a day after the Quad leaders' summit in Manila, Philippines and as India hosts a joint humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) exercise involving the four member countries

Mr. Singh and Mr. Jaishankar will co-chair the Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue (2+2) with their Japanese counterparts, Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement.

articles.title: Gilead signs generic licensing deals for experimental Ebola drug
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings

Gilead Sciences said on Monday it had signed royalty-free deals with three generic drugmakers to make its experimental Ebola prevention drug available in 127 mainly low- and lower-middle-income countries if it succeeds in trials and wins regulatory approvals.

The deals with Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, Eva Pharma and Ferozsons Laboratories cover obeldesivir, and include all African countries reporting cases in the current Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak. Obeldesivir has shown activity against several Ebola-related viruses in preclinical studies but is not approved for any use in any country.
A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings.

Gilead is also expanding remdesivir licences to cover Ebola-related diseases if trial results are positive and regulators approve the drug. The company has donated more than 38,000 remdesivir vials to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and Kenya, including more than 2,000 recently sent to Kenya for investigational treatment and post-exposure prevention.
Remdesivir is not approved to treat or prevent Ebola Bundibugyo disease, and its clinical effectiveness has not been established.

articles.title: CCMB study points to new way of tackling fungal infections
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Fungi can gradually develop resistance to current antifungal drugs, making infections increasingly difficult to treat

Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, have identified a promising new strategy to combat fungal infections by preventing disease-causing fungi from becoming invasive, rather than killing them outright.

Most current antifungal drugs work by destroying fungal cells. However, fungi can gradually develop resistance to these medicines, making infections increasingly difficult to treat. A team led by Sriram Varahan at CCMB studied ‘Candida albicans’, a fungus commonly found on human skin and in the body. While generally harmless, it can cause serious infections when it enters the bloodstream or internal organs.

The researchers focused on ‘morphogenesis’, in which the fungus changes from a round-cell form into long, filament-like structures, a transformation allowing the pathogen to evade the body’s immune defences and spread more effectively within tissues.

Earlier studies had shown that glycolysis, the process through which cells metabolise sugar, plays a key role in controlling this shape change. Building on these findings, the team screened a library of small molecules that target glycolysis and identified two compounds capable of blocking the transformation.

Although the fungus continued to grow, it remained in its harmless rounded form suggesting that the compounds could serve as “anti-infective” agents that reduce the fungus’ ability to cause disease without necessarily eliminating it.

The study also identified pyruvate kinase, an enzyme involved in sugar metabolism, as a crucial regulator of fungal morphogenesis. Researchers further found that one of the compounds reduced biofilm formation, a protective layer that helps fungi resist treatment. The compound also increased the effectiveness of widely used antifungal drugs such as fluconazole and amphotericin B.

In a mouse model of systemic Candida infection, treatment with the lead compound significantly improved survival rates, highlighting its potential for future therapeutic development. “Our findings suggest that fungal disease-associated behaviour can be targeted without necessarily stopping fungal growth,” said Dhrumi Shah, first author of the study. “We need further studies to evaluate the compounds effectiveness and safety but by blocking the fungus from becoming invasive, they could complement existing treatments,” said Sriram Varahan.

The findings, published in ACS Infectious Diseases , emerged from a collaboration between CSIR-CCMB and the BRIC-Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, said a press release on Tuesday.
